Research, three prototypes and a strategy, 1 to 4 October 2026

Agents can already write CAD. The product is what proves the design.

This notebook gathers the work on one question: what an agentic engineering product should be, and why anyone would use it instead of a general coding agent. It holds a reading of 54 CAD-model papers, three working prototypes and the current strategy, which cites 266 sources. They reach the same answer. Generation is becoming free, so the scarce thing is evidence that a coupled mechanical, electrical and firmware design meets its requirements, first by checks and then on a bench.

Where it stands: the strategy is at revision B, a draft for review. Meridian runs locally with 237 Python tests passing. Datum has nine packages built and 991 tests passing, and the layer that joins them is designed and not yet built. Morrow's workspace redesign was exercised at desktop and phone sizes. No hardware has been built or bench-tested. What exists has the detail.

The short answer

You asked how the app beats Claude Code with computer use on SolidWorks, Fusion or KiCad. That agent is the easy baseline. Two GUI agents, GPT-5 and Qwen3.5-9B, completed 0.0% of ComAct's SolidWorks tasks in August 2026. The best GUI agent, GPT-5.4, completed 35 of CADWorld's 200 FreeCAD tasks in September. On Markov's own AutoCAD Bench, a vendor benchmark, seven frontier models scored between 0% and 46% of 50 tasks in mid-2026 runs.47, 49, 78 With GUI access only, GPT-6 Astra laid three short trace segments in an hour of KiCad.81

The competitor that matters is the same model writing code. A coding agent writes build123d, FeatureScript, Fusion TypeScript, atopile or KiCad files against a kernel or a vendor MCP. On CAD Arena's 18 parts, rebuilt through native CAD APIs, Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code scored 0.750 and GPT-6 Astra in Codex 0.671 on 25 September. On CADBench V3's 100 FreeCAD tasks the same Opus 5.5 setup scored 61.03 on 24 September.76, 77 On EEBench's 13 circuit tasks, with three attempts each, Claude Opus 5.5 scored 75.0 ±8.3 and GPT-6 Astra 69.3 ±10.7 on 29 September.74 Fusion Compute MCP, Flux MCP, Siemens' Questa One MCP and 223 community KiCad MCP repositories are turning tool access into a commodity within about a year.90, 141, 150, 182

Rev A said an agent-for-CAD app competes with the model labs. That overstated it. No lab ships a CAD or EDA product. The risk from the labs is capability drift in code-CAD and circuit design. Anthropic's and Google's terms also forbid using their services to build a competing product.87, 89 Both facts argue for a command-line environment that any vendor's agent can drive.

The product is therefore three assets that nobody holds together today. The physical loop comes first.

  • A physical loop. Bench results are written back into the catalogue. This moves from the fifth move in Rev A to the first. Every published check suite can be gamed, every simulation has a model gap, and hardware on a bench is the only verifier that closes the gap between the written requirement and what was meant.19, 28
  • A cross-domain source tree. Requirements compile into deterministic checks and into bench plans, across the motor, reducer, board, housing and firmware.
  • A registry of verified modules. Each module carries measured curves, a license class and an executable interface, and it covers vendor actuators and custom designs alike.

Two moves follow.

  • Demonstrate it on the actuator, and let the actuator fail. Recomputed with the motor's datasheet curve and published reducer measurements, the Rev A example misses its torque requirement at speed on 24 V by about 2x, and by about 2.7x if the datasheet axis is oz·in.203, 207 The environment should report that before a person computes it.
  • Own a held-out eval set with repeated attempts. Three attempts on 13 tasks give the leading models on EEBench standard errors of 6 to 12 points.74 Your set needs more attempts, impossible tasks and an audited false-done rate.

What the evidence rules out, and what a general agent still lacks

You asked why anyone would use this instead of Codex, or instead of GPT-6 Astra driving Onshape. The research, and three reviewers asked to attack the first draft, changed the answer. Most of the obvious pitches are already taken.

What the evidence rules out

  • "Our agent drives CAD better than computer use." True, and beside the point. Computer-use agents finish 17.5% of FreeCAD tasks against 87% for experts, but nobody will click a GUI when Fusion and Onshape expose headless tools to Codex.
  • "Our agent writes code-CAD with a render loop." That is an open-source server and a 16.6k-star Codex plugin today.
  • "AI that designs the board and its enclosure." Flux shipped it on 24 September.
  • "A new place where engineers author everything as code." Professionals will not move their CAD.

What a general agent still lacks

  • Facts that are in nobody's weights. What this printer does to a 3.4 mm hole. This motor's torque at 600 rpm on 24 V.
  • A check the generator did not write. A model grading its own design shares its own blind spots.
  • Contracts at the seams. Fusion syncs a board outline. Nothing checks that the driver can feed the motor, or that the firmware's pin table matches the schematic.

Generation is becoming free, which makes assurance the scarce thing. So the product is not the agent. It is the layer every agent reports to.

The landscape

What you are up against

Three groups matter. The model labs set a baseline that moves every month. The CAD and EDA vendors are opening their tools to every agent. Funded specialists each hold one domain, and a few systems of record hold requirements and test data without authoring designs.

The baseline is a coding agent, and it moves monthly

Code beat clicking in every comparison found. On ComAct's 1,000 SolidWorks, Inventor and AutoCAD tasks, published on 24 August, GUI agents scored 0.0% while agents writing COM code reached 74% to 88% success.47 On EngiWorld's 1,301 tasks across 26 tools, published on 29 September, all seven models scored higher through a command line than through a GUI. DeepSeek V4.1 went from 2.0 to 48.3.48 In September NextPCB gave GPT-6 Astra a KiCad board. With full tool access it finished in about 12 minutes, because Freerouting did the routing and Astra ran the workflow. With keyboard and mouse only, it laid three short trace segments in an hour.81

The leader among code-driving agents changes month to month. GPT-6 Astra led EEBench from 4 September until Claude Opus 5.5 was added on 29 September. The leaderboard file estimates Astra at about $0.83 and 106 s per task, against about $2.37 and 802 s for Opus 5.5.74 On CADBench V3's 100 tasks on 24 September, Opus 5.5 scored 61.03 in Claude Code and 57.96 in mini-swe-agent. The 3-point gap comes from one run each with no published standard error, so it may be noise.77 Do not bet the product on one vendor's model.

The labs ship models and no CAD tools

No lab ships a CAD or EDA product. The Fusion connector in Claude's directory is built by Autodesk.86 OpenAI's Astra launch page shows a 15-second condensed playback of a 2 min 54 s KiCad run, with no board size, DRC result or evaluation.83 Anthropic's only published CAD figure is BenchCAD Vision2Code. Opus 5.5 scores 0.730 on it without tools and 0.962 with a container and an image-cropping tool, so the benchmark is close to saturated.84 xAI is the only lab that says it trains on purpose-built CAD environments.85

The labs are buying data as well. Markov, a Y Combinator S26 company, says it has sold more than 15,000 hours of CAD screen recordings to frontier labs, a vendor claim.80 GUI competence will rise whatever you build. The threat from the labs is capability drift and their terms. Anthropic and Google forbid using their services to build a competing product or service, and Anthropic, OpenAI and Google all cap liability at 12 months of fees.87, 88, 89 A command-line tool that any agent can drive keeps you out of any single provider's clause.

Vendor MCPs are commoditising access

Autodesk shipped a local Fusion MCP in May, a Fusion Data MCP on 2 July and the Fusion Compute MCP public beta on 15 September.90 Each agent gets its own Fusion session in Autodesk's cloud. The server has eight top-level tools and three modes. Execute is the default mode, CRUD and CRUDE are the others, and a sessionless API index answers questions without starting Fusion.92 The figure of more than 7,000 endpoints is the size of Fusion's TypeScript API, which the Execute tool reaches.90 Beta limits are two concurrent sessions per user, a one-hour cap, a 15-minute idle stop and a boot of 30 to 90 s, and Autodesk says to expect them to change.91 Its launch demo runs four sub-agents at once, which the two-session cap does not allow a single user.

Electronics is named in the launch post's scope three times, and no electronics operation is documented anywhere. The Electronics API is a read-only preview with 139 objects. The 5,672-entry API reference has no simulation namespace.90, 93, 94 No price is stated, and access needs a Fusion licence and a Fusion Team hub.91 Fusion's own ECAD to MCAD link is three documents kept in step by out-of-date pulls, each one a GUI command.95 Autodesk's platform terms bar applications that “function substantially the same as any Developer Offering” and give Autodesk audit rights.96 Adam's hands-on review found that “nothing about Fusion MCP validates a design against physical constraints or your team's own standards.”101

The other mechanical vendors are moving the same way, more slowly. PTC shipped a deliberately narrow Onshape FeatureScript MCP on 11 August, with agents “coming soon.”97 Creo 13 shipped on 10 June with a chat assistant, a model-reading Assist mode in beta and an Automate mode in alpha that explains each change and asks before it proceeds.98 Dassault's Aura, Leo and Marie companions went live on 23 July with 19 competencies and no public agent API.99 SolidWorks still has no vendor endpoint. The largest community server, solidworks-automation-skill, has 1,057 GitHub stars.100

Electronics access is opening just as fast. Flux opened a public MCP server on 3 August.141 Siemens' Questa One toolkit ships MCP servers and names Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and Cline as clients.182 223 GitHub repositories match “kicad mcp,” and the largest has 2,561 stars.150 By 2027 access will differentiate nobody.

Zoo

You asked about Zoo. It is the one mechanical startup with its own geometry kernel, and today it is a part-level modelling assistant.

Engine

The engine is closed. On the self-serve tiers it runs only in Zoo's cloud, and the Design Studio view is a video stream from the hosted engine.125 Since February 2026 Zoo says enterprise customers can self-host the kernel, API and ML services in their own data centers, a vendor claim.117, 118 API and MCP use is metered at $0.0083 per second, which is $0.50 a minute. The free tier trains on user data with no opt-out.115

Scope

Assembly mates are listed as in progress for Q4 2026. Version control and drawings are listed for Q1 2027.116 Zoo's FAQ says Zookeeper cannot run physical tests, guarantee manufacturability or structural safety, or perform detailed engineering simulations.117

Agent

Zookeeper runs on OpenAI reasoning models with four tools plus snapshots and mass properties. Zoo publishes no success rates.119 Zoo's own Makeathon write-up called the agent's output on a historical drawing “incoherent.”120 Its MCP server has one idea worth copying. A mock_preflight tier checks a request before real_execution spends engine time.124

Terms

Zoo's terms forbid using the services to “develop, commercialize, license or sell any product” that could directly or indirectly compete. Building on its engine needs a negotiated agreement.121

Funding

Disclosed funding is a $5.1M Form D sale in March 2023. CB Insights puts the total at about $10.1M. A reported $30M round in 2025 could not be verified.122, 123

For youZoo competes for the same mechanical user and does not touch boards, firmware or the bench. The reusable asset is the MIT-licensed KCL language and its tooling. Treat KCL as a possible input format, and do not build on the engine without a contract.

Who holds each domain

Mechanical

Generators. Adam raised a $4.1M seed and charges $40 or $200 a month, with token cost passed through. It writes FeatureScript or Fusion Python and reads back screenshots.103 Its founders deleted their DSL and feature tools because “every abstraction we wrote was something the model had to fight around.”102 Adam's own test of a valid part is that “parts compile, constraints solve, references stay stable.”104 Leo has raised $9.7M.105 Hestus raised a $7.4M seed on 2 October for sketch autocomplete inside Fusion.106 Backflip, with a $30M Series A, turns scans, drawings and photos into editable CAD with feature history.107

Reviewers. CoLab's AutoReview checks drawings against ASME and ISO and against quantitative DFM thresholds. CoLab raised a $72M Series C on 10 November 2025 and says 47,000 people are on its waitlist.108, 109 bananaz, with a $5.3M seed, enforces Y14.5 on change sets.110 Dessia's Lagrangia agent generates temporary clearance volumes to test tool access, and Dessia writes that “generation without verification only moves the bottleneck.”111 Synera raised a $40M Series B on 14 April to orchestrate CAD, FEA and PLM with logged runs, and says it serves more than 60 enterprise customers.112 PhysicsX raised $300M at about $2.4B on 8 June for physics surrogates.113 Navier sets up simulations over open solvers.114

For youIn mechanical CAD, generation and verification sit in separate companies. The verifiers are better funded, and none of them designs.

PCB

Quilter. Quilter raised a $25M Series B on 6 October 2025. It takes a finished schematic and returns ranked layout candidates in native Altium, Allegro, Xpedition or KiCad files. It runs eight physics rule checks using IPC-2221 at a fixed 20 °C rise. Its documented envelope is at most 48 V, 10 A and 5,000 pins, and it does not check schematic logic or intent beyond what you specify.126, 127

Its Project Speedrun is the only published first-spin result with numbers, and all of it is a vendor claim. 843 components and 5,141 pins across an 8-layer module and baseboard took 38.5 hours of human cleanup against a claimed 428, for layout of an existing reference schematic, and 20 of 20 boards booted Linux.129 Hacker News readers called the 428 overestimated by about an order of magnitude.132 The fab review returned 58 DFM findings. 48 were documentation, library, BOM and supply-chain errors, and 10 touched the physical design.128

Diode and atopile. Diode raised $11.4M led by a16z. It sells designs at $10,000, $20,000 or $50,000 plus fab cost per unit, with bring-up in the Enterprise tier only.133 Its MIT-licensed Zener language ships check() assertions, TestBench path matchers over the circuit graph, a versioned registry and an agent sandbox per registry branch.134 Diode graded Claude's reference designs on properties such as at least 22 µF between power and ground.135 atopile, MIT-licensed with 4,000 stars, runs EEBench and sells simulation-backed training environments to labs. Its public repository has had no commits since 11 March 2026, while PyPI releases continued to 0.15.9 on 12 September.136, 137 That is a platform risk.

Flux. Flux is the closest to cross-domain. The $37M it announced on 27 February was a $27M Series B led by 8VC, closed in January, plus a previously undisclosed $10M Series A.138, 139 Its figures of 1,099,361 builders and 6,425,482 projects are cumulative sign-ups. Adafruit's complaint of 5 June alleges they were hard-coded and unchanged from at least 23 October 2025, and the counter no longer appears on the homepage.140 The MCP server of 3 August exposes pin assignments and net names so outside agents can write firmware headers. Design edits still go through Flux's own agent.141 On 24 September Flux began generating 3D-printable enclosures from the board, with cutouts, standoffs and vents kept in sync. The flow is board-first, with no STEP export, moulding or motor scope mentioned.142 Flux now says enclosure and mechanical design live inside Flux next to the schematic, layout and firmware.143

Incumbents and tools. Cadence announced AuraStack on 15 July for September availability, with consumption pricing on top of Allegro licences.144 Siemens announced Fuse on 16 March with no GA date.145 Altium Designer's release notes through 26.10 contain no AI feature.147 The Altium 365 Requirements Portal gained an Engineering Assistant that edits requirement text and executes nothing.146 Altium's MCAD CoDesigner syncs geometry both ways and derives nothing, and its 3.15.0 release lists no new features.148 Celus turns requirements into schematics, and Neurocad turns datasheets into symbols, footprints and 3D models.152, 153 Stock KiCad cannot be driven headlessly through its IPC API until KiCad 11, which also removes the SWIG bindings.149 Smaller entrants are arriving too. Nomoreda is a browser EDA tool built for agents, and its users bring the harness subscription they already pay for.154 Traceformer reviews schematics on paid plans from $20 a month and cites a datasheet page for every finding, a vendor claim.155 BoardMint runs a deterministic checker and uses AI only to explain the findings.156 Stillwind repairs footprints to IPC-7351B.157 HeyPCB runs a browser workspace where an agent writes KiCad-native schematics and layouts.158

The sharpest data point. JLCPCB tested GPT-6 Astra in EasyEDA Pro. DRC reported zero errors while the first import carried 50 association mismatches, 20 footprint and 30 schematic-to-PCB, because every 0603 capacitor used one footprint. JLCPCB's summary is that “a board can open normally and still contain 50 broken library associations.”82

For youBoard-level verification is the most advanced and still stops at the board edge. Flux crosses the edge in one direction, board first, with geometric sync. Your direction is motor first, with fit, thermal and torque checked against requirements.

Firmware

Embedder, a YC S25 company with J-Link flash and RTT across more than 500 platforms, calls itself “a context layer with custom tools.” Its claim of more than 10,000 engineers is a vendor claim.159 BootLoop, also YC S25, validates on oscilloscopes and logic analysers.160 HILstart, YC S26, builds an approved specification from schematic, layout, netlist, BOM and requirements, drafts executable tests for human approval and runs them on its Tracer box. Its rule is “hardware is read-only by default; actuation asks for your grant,” and its reports flag when two runs are not comparable.161

Simantic, YC F26 with about $600k raised, validates its firmware simulator by requiring that “deliberately broken firmware fails for the right reason.”162 Veecle Chiplab charges $0.02 per run on virtual STM32 and Nordic targets.163 Wokwi exposes an experimental MCP with 11 tools, and Memfault exposes 12 read-only tools.164, 165

For youNone of these stores the mechanical or electrical source. Each ingests it as context. The bench loop exists, and nobody has the design tree it should close against.

Chips

Startups. Ricursive, ChipAgents, Cognichip and Agentrys alone have raised about $520M. Ricursive raised a $300M Series A at a $4B valuation with no public product.173 ChipAgents has raised up to $134M and Cognichip $60M.174, 175 Agentrys raised $24.5M and claims more than 90% on NVIDIA's CVDP benchmark, with no published subset or denominator.177 The only public price is ChipNexus at $200 a month for 100M tokens, with a node-locked CLI.178

Incumbents. None of the three EDA vendors' agents is generally available. Synopsys plans GA of AgentEngineer at the end of 2026, citing more than 50 customer engagements and a vendor-quoted gain of up to 50x in verification closure.179 OpenAI and Synopsys announced GPT-Synopsys on 30 September, a model tuned to drive Synopsys tools, with early engagements only.180 Cadence's ChipStack Super Agent, announced on 10 February, is in early deployment.181 Siemens' Questa One toolkit is in early access and already ships MCP servers.182

Two end-to-end runs. Verkor's Design Conductor took a 219-word spec to a 1.48 GHz RV32I core on the predictive ASAP7 kit in 12 hours. It used tens of billions of tokens from an undisclosed model vendor and reported no DRC or LVS. Its authors write that “it will remain critical to have experienced human architects guide systems such as DC.”171 Hsu drove four RV32I cores to DRC-clean layouts on sky130 and ASAP7 with Claude Code and the ORFS Docker image for $9.80 and 2 h 34 min, one run per configuration.172

Harness ideas. Standard Machines sells chip-design RL environments with “no LLM judge anywhere in the reward path.”183 Agentrys' rule that “every claim is backed by an artifact that has a checksum in a machine-readable manifest” is the most reusable idea in this group.176

For youAdvanced-node chip design belongs to the vendors who own signoff. Copy the chip field's harness lessons. Use open shuttles to learn the flow, and stay out of the chip-agent market.

Across domains

Flow Engineering. Flow raised $50M at a $750M valuation on 30 September, with Valor and Atreides co-leading, to “build the leading AI harness for hardware engineering.”191 Its only live CAD connector is an Onshape property pull of lengths, masses and volumes. SolidWorks, NX, Fusion, Ansys and Altium 365 are listed as coming soon.193 It hands code authoring to Cursor and takes back a pull request, and no release note shows it producing CAD geometry. It charges $150 or $300 per editor per month, with a 500-requirement cap on Basic.194 Its founder writes that “in the next year, AI will move from integrating the work, to doing the work.”192

Trace.Space, AllSpice and Nominal. Trace.Space has raised $6M and launched Trinity, an agent harness, on 29 September.196 Its rule is that “nobody should ever set a requirement's verification status by hand,” because it “should fall out of the data.”195 AllSpice runs git, CI automations and the DRCY reviewer on ECAD from $34,800 a year for five or more designers.197 Its findings link to datasheet clauses, and it states that DRCY “does not approve designs.”198 Nominal raised an $80M B-2 at $1B on 5 March. It owns test data and an open instrument layer, Instro, built so you “write your test logic once, swap the hardware.”199, 200

Others. JuliaHub raised $65M on 30 April behind the line “Spec in. Design out.”201 Dalus, YC W25, sells AI systems engineering to hardware teams.202 Lyon Industries published the only documented cross-domain failure. A general agent with KiCad 10 produced seven routing candidates with clean native DRC and ERC, and one still carried an 85.2 mm path from the regulator input to its input capacitor. No hardware was built. Its conclusion states the component-contract idea in one sentence, that “a part number, symbol, footprint, and 3D body cannot remain independent clues.”151 Small open prototypes exist. WireStudio compiles one design.json to firmware, KiCad and OpenSCAD with a pin solver. Konnect drives KiCad 10's IPC API with 228 tools. Mouro runs five check tiers on the rule “don't trust what a tool says about itself.”166, 167, 168

For youFlow is the closest to this thesis and the best funded. It manages and verifies the output of other people's tools and authors nothing. Teams that build or integrate actuators have no product that checks the motor, board and firmware together.

Status by domain

Each product verifies one domain or records results from others. None derives the board and firmware from the motor or closes a bench loop into a design library. Status is as of 3 October 2026.

The gap

Nobody on this list authors a coupled design and proves it. Rev A said no PCB tool treats the housing or firmware as part of the design. Flux's enclosures and MCP make that wrong for the housing and partly wrong for firmware. It remains true for the motor.

The defensible gap has two parts. The first is derivation direction. Flux derives the case from the board. An actuator derives the board, the copper and the firmware constants from the motor and the reducer. The second is verification depth. Geometric sync keeps holes aligned. Nothing in the landscape checks fit, thermal limits and torque at speed against a requirement across all three domains, and nothing writes bench results back into the design library.

The evidence

Where agents fail today

Every 2026 benchmark shows the same funnel. Models write CAD, circuit and simulation code that runs. A much smaller share meets the stated requirement, and the agent rarely knows which share it is in. The literature also agrees that reliability comes from the environment, and that the environment's main job is verification.

Code that runs is the easy part

MUSE is the cleanest stage-by-stage funnel. On its 106 design instances in version 2 of 4 June 2026, judged by Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5 executed 77.36% of single-pass CadQuery scripts, produced valid geometry for 68.87% and reached a final design-intent score of 52.36%.38 Overlap-free, at 70.75%, was GPT-5.5's weakest geometry check, and it was also the weakest for the closed-source average of 60.4, 44.5 and 30.6. That average read 42.9, 30.7 and 20.3 in version 1, because four open-weight models had been filed as closed-source.38

Three limits apply. MUSE is a single prompted pass with no feedback, repair or simulation loop, so it says nothing about the effect of feedback. Its reference designs began as STEP seed models built by professional designers, were expanded by Claude Opus 4.7 and reviewed by people, and have never been manufactured. Its judge, Gemini 3.1 Pro, is also a contestant, and it agreed with human ratings at r = 0.713 to 0.835 on 20 instances.38

Strict compliance is rarer still. Hephaestus-CCX gave agents 50 engineering briefs with CalculiX checkers. 400 first attempts produced zero strict passes. Ten attempts at about 68 minutes per item reached 9 of 50, and lifted mean requirement pass from 38.8% to 60.5%.41 CADEngBench found that of 1,030 programs that executed across eight systems, 432 also met the stated engineering and DFM requirements. So 58.1% of executable outputs violated at least one requirement.42 ChatCFD reports 82.1% execution against 68.12% physical fidelity.70 RealCADBench measured assembly solid IoU of 0.23 against 0.41 for single parts at similar executability. Its Codex agent with GPT-5.5 raised executability to 1.00 and lowered the product-identity score by 6.98 points, because “agents prioritize fixing syntax/execution over preserving product identity.”53

The actuator sits in the worst-measured region. It has many parts, mating interfaces and exact dimensions.

Agents stop early and say they are done

EngiWorld's multi-software tasks succeeded in 6 of 168 attempts, 3.6%. Between 73.9% and 87% of failures came from agents declaring done without running a check, and EngiWorld does not split this share by interface.48 CADWorld's best GUI agent, GPT-5.4, completed 35 of 200 FreeCAD tasks, 17.5%. It scored 16.0% on the 25 assembly tasks, 4 of 25, and Claude Opus 4.8 scored 8.0%. Every model scored 0% on the 15 CAM, 3 FEM and 2 TechDraw tasks. Opus 4.8's runs cost $10.00 per task. An expert's single reference pass scored 87.0%, which the authors say is not a controlled human study. Opus 4.8 ran on an older computer-use tool, and GPT-5.5 and Opus 5 were not tested.49 On Markov's AutoCAD Bench, GPT-5.6 Sol passed 23 of 50 tasks and Claude Opus 4.8 passed none. Its evaluator scores the saved file and does not see construction history.78

Physics feedback helps, by less than Rev A said

The Berger et al. result is an ablation in Section 8.1 of a paper accepted at IJCAI-ECAI 2026. Its 110 designs were drawn from a nominal study of 500 load cases, four models and three runs. The reported p = 0.0008 is the one-sided Fisher value, and the two-sided value is 0.0016. The only integer cell sizes consistent with its Table 4 put 7, 4, 10 and 6 designs in the disabled arm, and the enabled-arm percentages do not reconcile exactly with 49 of 83. The risk ratio is 2.7x with a 95% interval of 1.3x to 5.5x, so the honest headline is +37 points.39 The code, prompts and dataset were promised at camera-ready, and the repository was still empty on 3 October.40

Hephaestus-CCX confirms the direction at a smaller size. Its second large jump came only when “detailed FEA feedback adds failure margins and identifies the relevant selector or load case.” It also found that Claude Opus 4.7 at xhigh effort regressed after feedback on single parts, from 32.7% to 31.4%, and that “higher reasoning effort does not consistently improve performance.”41 A planner and a budget are the levers. Berger's own planner ablation cut mean iterations from 10.77 to 4.44, with 80 runs in each arm and p = 0.0071.39

Feedback signals rank in a consistent order

Typed physics and executable tests come first, then solver state, then execution errors, then consensus, then visual critique. Representation sits under all of them.

Structured geometry beats pixels

OmniCAD is the largest assembly benchmark, with 25,000 real SolidWorks assemblies and 289,000 mates. Frontier VLMs given a part library and eight views placed parts within 10 mm 27.9% of the time one-shot and 34.6% with ten rounds of render and collision feedback. They recovered at most 46.1% of mate edges, and the best conflict-free rate was 43.8% even with conflict reports.45 The authors note poor scalability to large part libraries and tabulate no accuracy by part count. CADMate shows the part-count effect directly. A fine-tuned model's placement accuracy fell from 90.35% on 2 to 5 parts to 68.56% on 10 to 15.46

Structured inputs win. BrepCoder's face-adjacency graph gave an error-correction Chamfer of 0.335 against 350 to 400 for frontier models working from rendered images.52 3DHarnessBench found that camera-pose metadata gives the most consistent gains. Agent-controlled viewpoints raised Opus 5 from 0.725 to 0.927 and hurt Gemini 3.1 Pro. Adding bounding boxes and measured dimensions cut Chamfer from 0.0150 to 0.0103.50 Vision2CAD's ID-tagged renders, with dashed hidden edges and a local-coordinate bridge, lifted mIoU from 0.4187 to 0.4733.51

Renders still catch coarse faults. CADSmith's kernel-metrics loop reached 99% executability, and adding three views took mean Chamfer from 18.19 to 0.74. Its quadcopter frame still passed every check with small gaps between the arms and the hub that no view showed.44 CADWorld's GUI agents scored 0% on every CAM, FEM and TechDraw task, because those workflows show little intermediate state on screen.49 The harness should choose a curated set of views, attach numbers to every observation, and never treat visual review as the safety net.

The harness moves the score more than the model

StructureClaw's structured harness lifted nine models' pooled end-to-end success from 22.0% to 82.9% on 150 structural scenarios.65 Anthropic's own BenchCAD figure, 0.730 without tools and 0.962 with them for Opus 5.5, is the same effect on a lab's eval.84

Deng et al. is the strongest single result and the thinnest evidence. On one design, PicoRV32, and one commercial 55 nm flow, the same model scored 11.67 or 97.94 depending only on the harness. Gated completion of synthesis, physical implementation and ECO was 8/8, 7/8 and 3/8 for Claude Code. It was 8/8, 3/8 and 2/8 for Claude Code with marketplace EDA skills, and 8/8 on all three for FluxEDA, the authors' own research harness.9, 170 Commands that were valid syntax but wrong for the tool version, mode or state made up 31.7% of physical-implementation error events.170

The caveats are material. There is one run per configuration and one design. Tool versions are undisclosed, the tool was named in version 1 and redacted in version 3, and version 2 was withdrawn citing possible legal issues. The 141.2x spread in Token ROI, the paper's cost-efficiency measure, is between two failed runs with identical progress, $0.11 in 59 minutes against $29.77 in 472 minutes, and version 1 had reported 105.92x for a different pair. Nobody had cited or replicated the paper by 3 October.170

EEBench's methodology page says that in an unpublished 2x2 test the harness moved GPT-5.5 by more than the whole GPT-5.5 to 5.6 model delta. The only public yardstick for that delta is 2.9 points, 42.3 against 39.4, which sits inside both standard errors. The same page says OpenAI rows use a neutral API loop, and the live board runs every GPT-6 model under Codex CLI.74, 75

Agents game the graders they can reach

The reliability literature turns Rev A's “separate the judge from the builder” into a stricter rule. Checks must be deterministic first and out of the builder's reach. LLM judges miss about half of what matters.

The real-world failure is data consistency

Three separate reports point at the same failure class, two of them vendors describing their own tools. JLCPCB's Astra board had zero DRC errors and 50 broken library associations.82 Quilter's own fab review found that 48 of 58 DFM findings were documentation, library, BOM and supply-chain errors.128 Lyon Industries' agent passed native DRC and ERC with an 85.2 mm path from the regulator input to its capacitor.151 Checks that read one file at a time pass all three. A check tier that compares the part number, symbol, footprint, 3D body and BOM line for every component catches them in milliseconds.

Measure consistency as well as accuracy

In tau-bench's retail domain, GPT-4o's pass^1 of about 61% falls below 25% at pass^8, so a single successful run says little about the next one.34 METR's 80% time horizons are 5 to 8x shorter than its 50% horizons.22 EEBench's three attempts on 13 tasks leave the leading models with standard errors of 6 to 12 points, too wide to separate them.74 Most figures in this section are single runs on models released in 2026. They will rise. The pattern will not change. Agents hand over output that looks finished and fails a check they never ran.

The thesis

One test for every roadmap item

When the next model ships, does this item become more valuable or less?

Anthropic's harness team writes that “every component in a harness encodes an assumption about what the model can't do on its own,” and those assumptions go stale as models improve.1 A product made of such components shrinks with each release. A product made of things the model cannot supply grows, because better models produce more designs and every one still has to be proven.

The research since Rev A sharpens the test. Adam deleted its own CAD language and feature tools because the model had to fight every abstraction.102 Autodesk made code execution the default tool mode.92 Bash-only scaffolds of about 100 lines now exceed 74% on SWE-bench Verified.6 In LangChain's own test, adding unrelated tools dropped GPT-4o from about 55% to 2% on one calendar task.7 Hand-written action wrappers lose. Verifiers, state and typed references win.

Worth less with each model release

  • Prompt chains, planning scaffolds and teams of role-playing agents
  • Wrappers that drive another vendor's CAD through its screen or a hand-written action set
  • Tool access, which vendor MCPs now give away
  • Prose skill files, which can lower pass rates
  • Workarounds for today's weak spots, such as helpers for spatial placement
  • A chat panel added to an editor

Worth more with each model release

  • Checks calibrated against measured hardware, each with a published discrimination score
  • Verified modules with measured curves, license classes and executable interfaces
  • The record of predicted against measured for every build
  • Compiled standards and dated vendor capability packs
  • An eval set with canaries that lets you adopt a new model the day it ships
  • The place where designs are reviewed, signed off and ordered

Keep the left column thin and expect to delete it. Put the company's effort into the right column.

The thesis

Three assets, with the physical loop first

Rev A listed six moves in the order they pay off and put the physical loop fifth. The research moves it to first. The three assets are the physical loop, the source tree and the module registry. A command-line environment carries them to any agent, and bench-linked trajectories are a second revenue line.

Krentsel et al. name two gaps that no check suite closes. The requirement gap lies between the recorded requirement and what the stakeholder meant. The model gap lies between the environment's model and the world. Agents iterate against a fixed evaluator orders of magnitude faster than people, and each failure teaches them more about what the evaluator rewards.28 Published check suites get gamed, as the evidence above shows. Simulations have model gaps. RocketSmith flew four agent-designed rockets. The two with reported apogee reached 80% and 84% of prediction, and the failures came from ejection timing the model left out.64 A part on a bench closes both gaps.

Asset 1, first

The physical loop

Order boards and parts from inside the product, generate the bring-up plan with the design, and record what the bench measures. Instruments are read-only by default and actuation needs a grant, which is HILstart's rule.161 Every report links to its test script and firmware build hash and flags runs that are not comparable. Predicted against measured, check by check, is data no lab, benchmark or vendor has. It recalibrates the simulations, and every cause of a respin becomes a new check.

Polymer reducers show why it comes first. A PA12-CF disc passed a nominal stress check with ample margin and failed by thermal fatigue after 95,040 cycles.220 No check written before that test would have asked for a disc temperature.

Asset 2

One source tree whose requirements compile into checks and bench plans

Output torque at least 5 N·m at 30 rpm. Board clears its pocket by 0.5 mm. Driver junction below 110 °C at stall. Each compiles to an executable check with a unit, a limit and a margin, and to a bench step that measures the same quantity. A person signs the compile step, because models miss necessity and correctness defects in requirements essentially always.35 Back-translating the formal form into plain language lets the reviewer check it without learning the syntax, and with that feedback strong models reached 98% to 99% on NL-to-STL translation.36 Numbers come from solvers. An LLM asked to compute a worst-case delay directly got it right in 1 of 6 attempts.37 The compiler refuses any requirement without a measurable acceptance test, which is the lesson of Verkor's specification note.171

The tree carries typed ports and contracts. The board outline is an expression of the motor's bolt pattern. A trace's current rating refers to the motor's phase current. The firmware's counts per output revolution are encoder resolution times the reducer ratio. Ports and mates are typed and resolved by closed-form transforms, so the model never emits a coordinate it estimated from a render.62 Assume-guarantee contracts state what each module needs and promises, and the quotient operation derives the spec of the module that is missing.17 Change the ratio and everything downstream is derived and checked again.

Asset 3

A registry of verified modules

A closed-loop NEMA 17 driver ships as one package with a generator, typed ports, tests validated against mutants, a constraint tree, a license class and its bench record. Vendor actuators enter the same registry with their measured curves. Knowledge ships as executable, version-pinned interfaces. Seed the registry yourself, because the open actuator communities are small and partly dormant. ODRI's hardware repository was last pushed in September 2022.235

How it reaches people

A vendor-neutral command-line environment

Ship the toolchain as a command-line tool over text source files. Claude Code, Codex or any other agent can then build, check and diff a design. Your app adds review, visual diffs, parallel variants, parts data and ordering. Neutrality is also a contract question. A product bound to one lab's agent inherits that lab's competing-product clause.87, 89

Second revenue line

Trajectories with bench outcomes

Markov sells CAD environments with task statements, reference inputs, screen recordings, gold outputs, rubrics and action trajectories.79 Your runs produce the same fields plus a measured result, which is the one field no lab has. Sell that bundle once the bench corpus is large enough to matter.

The thesis

Fourteen mechanisms with measured effects

The papers and the competitors together supply mechanisms whose effects have been measured. A general agent on stock tools cannot reproduce any of them inside a session. Together they define a verified module. It is a parametric generator with declared ports and mates, requirement tests validated against mutants and a constraint tree. It also carries a rebuild test that changes one parameter and re-runs the tests, a license class, a record of past design cases the agent can retrieve, and a bench record.

Four additions specific to actuators

  • An actuator-family compiler. It emits a size series that shares one firmware, one debug tool and one spares list. RobStride sells such a series, Figure designs its own actuator family in-house, and Primo chose RobStride for “one firmware, one debug tool, one set of spares.”224, 227, 232
  • A buy-versus-build advisor. It automates Primo's motor-selection sheet, comparing reflected inertia at ratio, backdrivability, price, lead time and public CAD against the requirement.224
  • Bench templates from the literature. Doggo's continuous-torque test raises current until the stator settles at 125 °C in 22 °C ambient with no cooling.222 Roozing's protocol runs in for 90 minutes and measures play and friction before and after a 10-hour endurance block.217 ToddlerBot identifies nine parameters per motor.223 Polymer reducers add a disc-temperature log against a 50 to 70 °C bound.
  • License-class gating in the package manifest. The most copied NEMA 17 closed-loop designs are share-alike, non-commercial or unlicensed. Mechaduino is CC BY-SA, and the Smart Stepper firmware is GPLv3 for non-commercial use only.225, 226

The model question, from the 1 October research report

A CAD model that learns what a design must preserve

Before the strategy settled on an evidence layer, a separate report asked whether to train a CAD model at all, and which one. It is a larger paper review, a concrete training recipe and twelve startup hypotheses for agentic engineering. It is a research proposal, not a trained model or a validated business.

54
papers reviewed
52
read for methods and evaluation
43
papers dated 2024 to 2026
12
startup hypotheses

What the report would pursue

The strongest direction it found is a company that completes engineering changes across a product family. Its model learns from revisions, constraints, failed rebuilds and accepted engineering decisions. Generating an initial part becomes one capability within that business.

Start with a model for revisions within a narrow mechanical product family, coupled to an existing CAD kernel. The initial offer: give us an existing assembly, a requested change and the requirements that must remain true. Receive an editable revision and a review package showing what changed, what passed and what remains unresolved.

Choose one recurring workflow: motor and gearbox substitutions, configurable brackets and enclosures, or tooling variants for a manufacturer. The commercial hypothesis is that repeated revisions provide both a reason to pay and better training examples than isolated text-to-shape prompts. A customer should buy fewer engineering hours and less revision rework. The model is how you improve that result.

The report would first adapt a small pretrained code or vision-language model to a supported native CAD history or executable code representation, training generation, local edits, error diagnosis and preservation together. Deterministic tools should establish measurable geometric and constraint checks. Engineering acceptance still needs the appropriate reviewer or test process. Direct boundary-representation generation deserves a separate research branch for difficult imports or surfaces that the initial operation vocabulary cannot express.

The broad vision of mechanical design, PCB layout, ICs, robotics and simulation is a plausible long-term scope. It is a poor first training distribution. Those fields use different representations, verification tools and acceptance criteria. The first company should earn a place in one recurring engineering workflow, then expand through shared interfaces and evidence.

Research scope and method: 54 additional papers were reviewed, 52 of them through methods and evaluation. Proposed experiments, customer segments and acceptance thresholds are the author's judgments. Paper findings are linked and qualified. No application was built. The report narrows several novelty claims made in an earlier startup memo and an earlier strong-baseline CAD analysis, which are not part of this page.

What the expanded reading changes

Initial-looking opportunityWhat already existsThe harder question left to test
Automatic reusable design routinesDreamCoder, Stitch, babble, ShapeMOD and ShapeCoder learn libraries or abstractions.Can routines learned from revision outcomes preserve the correct relationships on unfamiliar engineering tasks?
Automatic CAD refactoringSzalinski restructures CAD programs, and shape-library work also refactors program structure.Can a replacement native history survive future edits better while preserving the present model and required references?
Assembly ports, factories and explicit intentASSEMCAD and CIT-CAD cover substantial parts of this architecture.Can a learned policy produce useful missing components and changes under real interface and preservation constraints?
Complete geometry around fixed input facesAutoBrep already demonstrates face-conditioned completion.Can completion also satisfy motion, manufacturing, functional dimensions and intended feature history?
Improve a CAD model using execution rewardsMultiple CAD models use execution, reconstruction rewards or iterative repair.Can the reward distinguish legitimate repair from quietly changing the specification?

These are research gaps suggested by the reviewed evidence, not claims of worldwide novelty or patentability. The underlying techniques should be treated as tools and baselines. A startup advantage would require better outcomes on customer work, efficient delivery and a learning loop competitors cannot reproduce by adding the same public tools.

Three findings shape the training plan. First, Doris et al.'s CAD-Coder reports a variant losing fillet capability after fine-tuning. A lower learning rate helps on a prescriptive example but hurts reconstruction. Second, PR-CAD, Appendix A.4 describes reducing an unrequested inner radius to make an outer-radius edit executable. Third, Template Programs shows how learning from a group of related examples can produce a shared generative structure. Together these motivate retained-capability tests, immutable requirements and family-level training.

The boundary-geometry papers also make a useful distinction. A valid solid, an editable construction history and a mechanically acceptable design are three different targets, and improving one does not improve the others. The paper atlas records each method's actual target.

Which CAD generation model to create

Define the output before choosing the network. "CAD generation" currently covers several materially different problems.

OutputModel approachGood first useMain limitation
Executable code using a CAD APIAdapt a pretrained code model, optionally adding images or geometric embeddings.Fast experiments, generation and edits using existing operations.Executable scripts can encode fragile references or inappropriate design relationships.
Native feature and constraint historyGenerate typed actions, references, expressions and feature parameters.Editable production-oriented workflows in one supported CAD backend.Requires reliable histories, richer supervision and a stable execution interface.
Boundary representation (B-rep)Autoregressive topology and geometry tokens, or structured diffusion with geometric reconstruction.Shape completion, reverse engineering, freeform surfaces.Learned surfaces are fitted approximations. Successful sewing does not recover intent or guarantee specified dimensions.
Parameters of a known design familyClassifier or regressor, conditional generative model, or search plus continuous optimization.Configurable products with a restricted, valuable design space.Its ceiling is the expressiveness of the family. Compare it against a conventional configurator.
Assembly or mechanism graphGraph generation plus geometry, placement and solver-guided search.Connections and mechanisms where topology matters more than surface appearance.Mate labels and physical behavior are ambiguous. Validity is substantially harder than fitting one part.

The first model: a 2 to 8B pretrained model adapted to code or native actions, with explicit units, preserved parameters, entity references and bounded edit patches. The size range is an experiment proposal, not an optimum established by the papers. Benchmark a small and a larger candidate under the same hardware and execution budget before committing.

These representation choices overlap. FeatureScript is executable code that can create native features. Other rerunnable CAD scripts may produce a solid without materializing a native feature tree. Do not describe exported boundary geometry as recovered native history unless that history actually exists in the target system.

A compact typed action format may help training and validation, but inventing a new public language is optional. Initially, lower actions into one existing backend. Track action IDs, native features, geometric entities and assembly occurrences. This correspondence is a substantive engineering problem, because topology changes can split, merge or delete entities. Test semantic selections and lineage, and mark ambiguous mappings. An imported STEP file can supply boundary geometry. It does not supply the original feature tree, so mark recovered history as inferred.

For multimodal input, begin with dimensions and multiple views where available. A photograph alone may not determine scale, hidden holes or intended fits, so represent unresolved alternatives explicitly. Add point-cloud or B-rep encoders when an ablation shows that they improve reference selection or geometry understanding beyond rendered views and native queries.

The longer-term model could learn a joint distribution over a program, its interfaces and its response to possible edits. That is a research hypothesis. An implementable first approximation is multitask training on generation, patching, reference selection, failure classification and predictions of which invariants an edit will violate.

The model question

A concrete training recipe

Ten steps, in order: define the output, prepare the data, adapt the model, train with feedback, and only then consider the direct B-rep path.

  1. Specify a narrow output contract

    Choose a backend, a supported operation set and one customer task. For a first mechanical workflow, useful operations might include sketches and dimensions, extrusion, revolve, holes, patterns, fillets, chamfers and simple assembly placement. The exact list should follow the selected workflow. Add a shell or loft when the task needs it and there is enough verified data, not to make an operation count look impressive.

    The training target should distinguish a new design, an authorized change, an unchanged requirement, a conflict and insufficient information. An example target is a patch that enlarges a mounting pattern while preserving a shaft axis, a bearing interface and the location of an electrical connector. Do not train the model to rewrite an entire long history for every small request unless that performs better in controlled tests.

  2. Build executable data, not just captions and meshes

    Each training example should have an instruction, a before-state, an allowed change, a candidate after-state and independently measured outcomes. Store the native document or reproducible program, backend and kernel versions, units, dependencies, persistent reference information, task constraints, renders, geometric measurements and a record of execution. Keep the provenance and permitted use of each source alongside the example.

    Use three complementary sources: licensed native histories, procedurally generated families with known relationships, and human-reviewed real revision episodes. Public corpora are useful for bootstrapping, but a downloaded shape is not permission to train or redistribute. CADFS provides unusually useful native-program evidence. EPICCAD's original industrial assets, in contrast, are not an openly downloadable training set. Dataset, code, model and CAD-platform terms are separate checks.

    Do not turn every random parameter perturbation into a positive edit. Include impossible requests, wrong references, missing information, suppressed features, nearly coincident geometry, disconnected solids and topology-changing edits. Pair a failed edit with its actual failure and a corrected result when available. Keep failures for training diagnosis. Do not silently discard them and later report validity on the surviving subset.

    The proposed pilot is 10,000 to 30,000 verified episodes across a few dozen authored families, followed by a larger experiment of 100,000 or more only if the pilot produces a held-out gain. These numbers are planning hypotheses. A large number of variants from ten templates remains ten sources of structural diversity.

  3. Split by origin before generating variants

    Separate training, development and final evaluation by original design family, source document and customer organization where relevant. Cluster near-duplicate geometry and related histories into the same split. All perturbations, paraphrases, renderings and revisions of one original belong with it. Reserve unfamiliar combinations of known operations, unfamiliar operation types and long edit sequences as separate evaluation slices.

    Keep final human requests and acceptance decisions away from both generator and reward development. Count independent families when estimating uncertainty. Thousands of nearly identical examples do not justify narrow confidence intervals about new products.

  4. Establish a strong untrained baseline

    Before fine-tuning, give a strong general model the native API, exact geometry queries, examples, retrieval, persistent project state and the same repair budget. Also run the chosen small base model without adaptation. Add a conventional template or optimizer baseline for a family-specific task. Otherwise improvements may come from better tools, extra trials or a simpler problem rather than from the trained model.

  5. Supervised adaptation with capability retention

    Begin with supervised training on successful executable programs and localized edits. Use ordinary next-token training for code and actions. Add auxiliary reference-selection or parameter losses only when their labels are trustworthy. Where several programs are equally valid, accept multiple verified targets or use outcome-based selection, rather than penalizing all alternatives to one arbitrarily chosen sequence.

    As an initial ablation, mix roughly 40% generation, 35% edits, 15% diagnosis, repair and conflict handling, and 10% retained coding and less-common CAD operations. Those percentages are a starting proposal, not a published recipe. Compare the mix with task-only adaptation, and track capabilities such as fillets, expression use, loops and operation composition throughout training.

    Start with adapter tuning to make the experiment cheap and reversible, and compare full fine-tuning only if underfitting is visible. Tune learning rate and stopping on development-set engineering scores, not only token loss. Document seeds, sequence lengths, truncation, optimizer state and exact checkpoints. A long output cut off mid-feature is an operational failure, even if the preceding tokens were accurate.

    A first SFT experiment, proposed. Use assistant-output-only token loss, a minimal patch target and family-balanced batches. On a small development run, compare LoRA rank 16 against 64 and learning rates of 2×10−5 against 1×10−4, for one to three epochs. Choose context length from measured history lengths, starting with an 8,192-token experiment only if it covers the intended tasks and fits the hardware. Retrieve relevant dependencies for longer models, and never silently truncate protected requirements. Select checkpoints on development acceptance, capability retention and cost, then run the frozen final test once. These settings are an initial search grid, not a published optimum.

  6. Preserve numerical meaning

    Store dimensions with units and task tolerances. Keep explicit dimensions and equations authoritative when images are ambiguous. Separate coarse geometric tokens from high-precision parameter values if quantization is needed. Test the whole conversion chain: native document, training representation, generated representation, native rebuild, measured dimensions.

    Rounding that is harmless for a preview can collapse a narrow wall or break a sketch. The CADFS release itself notes that its reduced-precision scripts can fail to compile. Either maintain sufficient precision or measure and reject the resulting error. Never report a unitless Chamfer improvement as proof that a specified fit is correct.

  7. Use execution to improve the dataset

    PLAD supplies an important pattern: pair a proposed program with the geometry it actually executes to produce. If a generated program only approximately matches an original shape, distinguish that approximation from a true label. Keep both cases, with different training roles. Iterative search and self-training can specialize a model without a differentiable CAD kernel.

    For engineering edits, extend this pattern with preservation tests. A candidate enters the positive revision set only when it satisfies the requested change and every checked invariant. When the instruction is impossible under those invariants, a correctly diagnosed conflict is a useful target. Human review is still needed for requirements the tools cannot measure.

    Use a queue of specific failures to select new data: ambiguous references, operation combinations, thin geometry, unit confusion and changes spanning multiple parts. Measure coverage and failure reduction after each acquisition round. This is a more useful growth rule than continually generating easy random extrusions.

  8. Add reinforcement learning after the evaluator is trustworthy

    RL is appropriate when the desired outcome is measurable but a unique correct program is unavailable. It should follow a competent initial policy and a tested evaluator. Use bounded candidates and explicit failure reasons. Compare against equally expensive rejection sampling and self-training before attributing benefit to RL itself.

    suggested acceptance rule
    execution succeeds
  AND the requested change passes
  AND protected requirements pass
  AND the output remains editable under the selected tests

    Only then optimize secondary scores such as speed, code simplicity, material use or shape similarity. A weighted average can otherwise trade away an essential constraint for a prettier or easier solid.

    The hard acceptance gate is different from the training reward. If difficult tasks produce no successful rollouts, use easier curricula, guided examples or partial-progress rewards while continuing to prohibit acceptance until hard requirements pass. Inspect whether reward shaping teaches shortcuts. Compare RL against the same amount of search followed by supervised learning.

    Some constraints cannot be decided reliably by the available solver. Preserve "unknown" as a separate outcome, because a timeout or failed convergence is not proof of impossibility. The generator should never be able to edit the evaluator, delete a protected requirement or relabel a failed check as optional.

    A separate reward-model audit should include adversarial examples: deleting the difficult feature, changing units, shifting a protected interface, producing a trivial empty solid, suppressing a failing body and exploiting a coarse sampling grid. Use exact or conservatively bounded checks where available, and disclose sampling limitations elsewhere.

  9. Train for sequences of changes

    Single-turn reconstruction is too weak a target for an engineering company. Train on histories with multiple user revisions, and evaluate long sequences without restoring the correct intermediate state after every step. Include return edits, such as enlarging then shrinking a parameter, and branching requests where earlier decisions need to be reconsidered.

    The distinctive research question is whether training on future-edit behavior produces better present histories. Compare two models trained on identical initial geometry. One learns only current fit. The other also trains on subsequent edit episodes from the training families. Evaluate both on the same hidden edits and unfamiliar families. Improvements must survive a baseline with the same tools and constraints.

  10. If you choose direct B-rep generation

    Collect licensed solids with face-edge-vertex incidence, orientation, trims and analytic surface metadata. Preserve original units alongside normalized learning coordinates, and split families before augmentation. Reproduce an available implementation before changing its architecture. One route learns local surface and curve codes and predicts them autoregressively with connectivity references, as in AutoBrep and BrepGPT. Another predicts topology and denoises geometry conditioned on it, as in DTGBrepGen.

    First test the geometry encoder and decoder by round-tripping real parts through reconstruction and the kernel. If this stage loses a critical interface, a better generative prior cannot recover the lost precision. Then train unconditional generation, followed by partial-geometry, point-cloud or image conditioning. Fit surfaces and trims, construct and validate solids, and report results both before and after bounded repair. Treat exact dimensions and fixed interfaces as additional conditioning and validation experiments.

    Evaluate reconstruction error on protected surfaces, small-feature retention, topology validity, full-solid validity, candidate count and repair time. Keep history recovery as a separate task, because many construction sequences can create the same boundary geometry. This branch is justified when it solves a valuable geometric capability the code or history model cannot express.

What the published compute says

These are different tasks and architectures. The numbers establish possible experiment scales. They do not give a like-for-like cost ranking or a budget guarantee.

Paper and taskReported setupArithmetic and limitation
CAD-Coder
Pretrained VLM adaptation		4 H100 × (4.5 + 5.7) hours40.8 H100-hours. Original alignment and CAD stages. Excludes base pretraining and data.
CADmium
Code-model adapters		4 A100 80GB × 8 to 12 hours per run32 to 48 A100-hours per run. Does not include the large annotation workload.
CADFS
2B native-program model		8 A100 × (30 + 76) hours848 A100-hours. Two training stages. The stated memory use of 24GB per device is not a universal requirement.
PLLM
Execution-based self-training		4 L40S, about 150 hours elapsedGPU utilization not established. Most reported cycle time goes to sampling and to execution and selection.

Direct boundary generation		8 RTX4090D, 1 day tokenizers + 4 days decoder960 allocated GPU-hours if all 8 are used throughout. ABC training schedule. Allocated device-hours are not measured utilization.
