Direct geometry research baseline		Author guide: 2 RTX3090 for about 4 daysAbout 192 allocated GPU-hours. Implementation estimate only. The full paper was inaccessible.

The GPU-hours are simple arithmetic where device count and elapsed time are both given. They exclude base-model pretraining and usually exclude data preparation, failed runs and much evaluation. Hardware models are not interchangeable, and none are converted to cloud prices.

For a pilot, first measure a small end-to-end run: examples per second, tokens per example, native rebuild time, rejection rate and evaluation cost. Estimate supervised training time from actual token throughput. Budget RL across all iterations: rollout tokens, prompts × candidates × execution time, reward evaluation and policy updates. GPU and kernel work may overlap, so measure critical-path wall time instead of adding theoretical durations. Slow CAD execution, API rate limits and evaluator latency can dominate training.

A reasonable planning sequence is one adapter-training experiment that fits available hardware, a measured learning curve at two dataset sizes, and then a larger run. Direct B-rep training from scratch should be justified by a capability the code model cannot provide. Training a foundation model from scratch is unnecessary to test the proposed startup advantage.

What would count as a model advantage

MeasureWhat to reportFailure it catches
Execution and geometryFirst-attempt and bounded-retry validity, kernel failures, topology consistency and dimensional error.Programs that look plausible but do not build correctly.
Instruction completionExplicit requirements passed, failed or unknown, and human acceptance on ambiguous requests.Good shape similarity with the wrong requested change.
PreservationProtected dimensions, interfaces, dependencies and unrelated features retained.PR-CAD-style repair by changing something the user did not authorize.
Future editabilitySuccess under unseen parameter edits and feature changes, and reference survival across a sequence.A technically executable but fragile or misleading construction history.
Assembly functionRelevant mating, motion, clearance and task-specific analysis with stated assumptions.Correct isolated parts that fail together.
Human burdenReview minutes, manual corrections, time to accepted revision and unresolved questions.An automated pipeline that merely shifts work into checking.
Economics of inferenceTotal model calls, candidates, solver time, wall time and cost per accepted output.Winning by spending substantially more hidden computation.

Give the trained specialist and the general-model agent the same input information and the same permitted tools. Report single-sample results separately from best-of-k results, and include all failed attempts in time and cost. Evaluate cold-start tasks and repeated-family tasks separately, because amortized learning can benefit the latter without solving the former. Report completion and coverage alongside preservation, so that a model that refuses every task cannot appear successful. Test whether STOP, requests for clarification, rollback and "unknown" are used appropriately.

The proposed early gate is a meaningful reduction in median engineer review-and-correction time, with no increase in protected-requirement violations, across independently held-out families. A 25% time reduction is a useful planning target, not an established market threshold. Predeclare a sample size after a pilot estimates variance, and use paired tasks and confidence intervals. If gains disappear when the general model gets the same library and execution budget, the evidence supports an infrastructure product rather than a superior model.

A second gate is whether training changes the economics. A smaller model that matches acceptance at lower total cost can be valuable even if its maximum quality is lower. A benchmark gain that disappears in real review effort is not a sufficient reason to build a model company.

The model question

Twelve startup hypotheses

These are proposed combinations and business positions. The papers establish components of technical feasibility. They do not establish willingness to pay, so each idea needs both a technical comparison and a customer test. Open one to see its buyer, first test and reason to stop.

01First choiceEngineering changes that preserve the rest of the productDeliver an editable revision plus evidence that protected interfaces and dimensions remain correct.
Buyer
Mechanical engineering leads at manufacturers with recurring component substitutions.
Business hypothesis
Paid pilot followed by a recurring workflow contract, with volume tied to accepted revisions. Pricing and willingness to pay need interviews.
Possible advantage
Permissioned revision histories, engineer rejection reasons, and measured preservation outcomes can train a better policy within repeated product families.
First test
Compare accepted-revision time against the customer's process and a strong general-model agent on unfamiliar cases.
Reason to stop
Stop the model thesis if gains vanish with matched tools; stop the workflow thesis if revisions are infrequent or review consumes all savings.

PR-CAD exposes preservation failures; CADFS and EPICCAD support richer histories. CIT-CAD already covers intent trees and locked constraints. PR-CAD · CADFS · A multimodal benchmark for editable constraint preserving history based CAD modeling · CIT-CAD

02First choiceA compiler that learns a manufacturer's product familiesLearn a reusable parametric family from approved variants, then generate editable variants from requirements.
Buyer
Engineering and applications teams selling configurable brackets, housings, fixtures, or similar product lines.
Business hypothesis
Charge for family onboarding and recurring use across quoting, customization, and engineering changes.
Possible advantage
Learned allowed variations and exceptions become more valuable than a library of static models. Distribution can follow one manufacturer's existing configurator workflow.
First test
Hold out an entire variant branch; compare against an engineer-authored configurator and a general model given the same examples.
Reason to stop
If authoring a normal template is cheaper and equally reliable, sell conventional automation or choose a less templated problem.

Template Programs, ShapeMOD, and GeoCode precede family learning and parameter coupling. Learning industrial allowable changes is the proposed extension. Learning to Infer Generative Template Programs for Visual Concepts · ShapeMOD · GeoCode

03High-value researchGenerate the missing component from its interfacesGiven two or more fixed interfaces, available space, loads, and process constraints, propose the adapter, bracket, or connecting mechanism.
Buyer
Robotics integrators and mechanical designers repeatedly connecting purchased components.
Business hypothesis
Begin with an assisted design service in one component class; recurring access follows repeat use and qualified reusable designs.
Possible advantage
A learned proposal model could improve feasible-candidate yield before expensive validation. Accepted interface-to-part examples are the key data.
First test
Use unseen interface combinations and matched solver budgets; measure complete accepted candidates per unit compute.
Reason to stop
Reject the thesis if it mostly retrieves standard adapters or cannot outperform deterministic templates plus optimization.

AutoBrep already preserves input faces; assembly-port and mate-prediction work already exists. The proposed gain is functional and editable completion, not face completion itself. AutoBrep · ASSEMCAD · JoinABLe

04Promising narrow wedgeRepair the future editability of legacy CADRebuild or refactor a supported portion of a model, then demonstrate that specified future changes work.
Buyer
Engineering teams maintaining imported models or brittle inherited feature histories.
Business hypothesis
Charge for a migration or remediation project, followed by ongoing change support. Verify recurring demand before treating it as SaaS.
Possible advantage
Learn which histories survive real revision sequences, with clear boundaries around inferred and preserved geometry.
First test
Keep present geometry equal; ask independent engineers to perform hidden revisions on original and reconstructed histories.
Reason to stop
If reconstruction requires as much manual work as remodeling, narrow the operation coverage or abandon the general importer.

Szalinski, ShapeCoder, and TransCAD make generic refactoring or history recovery established prior art. Future-edit survival is the differentiating target. Synthesizing Structured CAD Models with Equality Saturation and Inverse Transformations · ShapeCoder · TransCAD

05Lower model riskIndependent regression testing for CAD changesDetect unintended consequences of a revision and provide reproducible evidence before review.
Buyer
Teams introducing agents or automation into an existing engineering release process.
Business hypothesis
A recurring validation service integrated with the customer's revision workflow; commercial demand is untested.
Possible advantage
A growing corpus of realistic failures, trusted task-specific checks, and integration into acceptance decisions. The generator can come from any vendor.
First test
Seed realistic errors and test detection, false alarms, and review minutes against the customer's existing checks.
Reason to stop
If ordinary native checks catch the same errors with similar effort, there is little standalone value.

Constraint-aware generation and explicit-history benchmarks motivate the checks; they do not establish an independent release evaluator. CIT-CAD · DAVINCI · A multimodal benchmark for editable constraint preserving history based CAD modeling

06Good model experimentA specialist model for failed CAD operationsExplain a localized kernel failure and propose the smallest authorized repair.
Buyer
CAD automation teams and engineers losing time to failed rebuilds.
Business hypothesis
Sell a workflow integration or API where measurable rebuild recovery saves time; first prove value in one backend.
Possible advantage
Failed operation traces, geometric witnesses, corrected outcomes, and rejected collateral changes are scarce, task-specific supervision.
First test
Give both specialist and general agent identical errors and geometry. Compare full recovery, collateral changes, and total tool time.
Reason to stop
If a few deterministic rules solve most cases, use those rules rather than forcing an ML business.

Iterative repair and residual-geometry generation already exist. Preservation-aware diagnosis on real native failures is the proposed focus. IterCAD · PS-CAD

07Research-heavyLearn intent by asking about consequential alternativesShow the smallest set of alternative edits that distinguishes what must remain fixed, then build the chosen relationships into the model.
Buyer
Teams reverse engineering ambiguous legacy parts or configuring products with incomplete requirements.
Business hypothesis
A capability within family onboarding or legacy conversion; standalone demand is weaker.
Possible advantage
Labeled choices about future behavior reveal intent that a static mesh cannot. The hypothesis is that selecting the right question cuts expert annotation time.
First test
Compare adaptive questions, a fixed checklist, and unrestricted chat by review time and correctness on later hidden edits.
Reason to stop
If questions increase effort without improving future behavior, keep a conventional requirements workflow.

Family programs and constraint prediction support candidate generation; they do not solve efficient elicitation of engineering intent. Learning to Infer Generative Template Programs for Visual Concepts · DAVINCI · GeoCode · Mates2Motion

08Specialized deep technologyA motion-to-mechanism company in a bounded design classTranslate a motion specification into candidate linkage topology and dimensions, then qualify feasible candidates for a selected use.
Buyer
Automation engineers designing repetitive planar motion mechanisms.
Business hypothesis
Sell completed mechanism studies or a recurring synthesis workflow in one motion class.
Possible advantage
Combine learned topology proposals, continuous optimization, and customer-specific physical constraints. The value is accepted mechanism performance.
First test
Compare with an expert and strong search baselines using identical simulation budgets and complete mechanical checks.
Reason to stop
Stop if the industrial task lies mostly outside the represented mechanism class or simulation validity fails to predict useful prototypes.

LInK and LinkD already combine learning with mechanism search. Their bounded planar results do not establish load, collision, tolerance, or manufacturing acceptance. LinkD · LInK · LINKS

09Enabling businessPermissioned engineering-history data infrastructureConvert authorized histories and revision episodes into versioned, executable, deduplicated training and evaluation sets.
Buyer
CAD vendors, model builders, and large engineering organizations with usable but disorganized native histories.
Business hypothesis
Data preparation contracts or private infrastructure subscriptions; buyers and procurement cycles need validation.
Possible advantage
Rights-cleared access, reproducible native execution, meaningful family splits, and verified change labels. A public-data scraper has much less differentiation.
First test
Train matched models on raw versus curated data and measure new-family acceptance per annotation hour.
Reason to stop
If organizations cannot grant usable rights or improvements are limited to in-distribution reconstruction, the proposed value weakens.

CADFS shows richer histories can matter; EPICCAD exposes industrial-access constraints; procedure-guided augmentation offers a supplement. CADFS · A multimodal benchmark for editable constraint preserving history based CAD modeling · Learning From Design Procedure To Generate CAD Programs for Data Augmentation

10Strong research complementGenerate the tests that break a CAD modelDiscover parameter changes and operation sequences that expose fragile references, false constraints, or silent specification drift.
Buyer
CAD model teams and engineering groups qualifying reusable design templates.
Business hypothesis
Start as a validation module for family compilers or CAD model evaluation; consider a standalone service only with repeat demand.
Possible advantage
Learn a distribution of consequential failures rather than sampling arbitrary geometry. Feed hard examples back into generation training.
First test
At fixed test budget, find more independently confirmed failures than random perturbation, property-based rules, and general-model test generation.
Reason to stop
If simple boundary-value sweeps find the same failures, keep the tool simple and focus the business elsewhere.

DAVINCI supplies constraint-preserving augmentation; repair papers supply erroneous trajectories. Adversarial future-edit selection is the proposed research combination. DAVINCI · IterCAD

11Best expansion from mechanical workQualify electromechanical component substitutionsCoordinate the mechanical revision with electrical interfaces and a task-specific verification plan.
Buyer
Small robotics and equipment manufacturers facing motor, driver, connector, or board changes.
Business hypothesis
Paid change cases followed by a recurring product-family service. The initial workflow should cover a small set of well-understood substitutions.
Possible advantage
Cross-domain dependency data and accepted change evidence can accumulate across revisions. Merely connecting two editors is easy to copy.
First test
Replay historical substitutions and prospectively measure total engineering effort, escaped interface errors, and cost of review.
Reason to stop
If cases are too bespoke to repeat or require extensive new physics each time, treat it as consulting rather than scalable software.

The earlier mechanical, electronics, and verification review supports the component methods. No reviewed paper demonstrates this complete commercial workflow. Earlier primary-paper notes

12Longer-term research branchTurn unfamiliar geometry into a documented editable subsetRecover supported analytic geometry and native history where possible, while clearly exposing unresolved or freeform regions.
Buyer
Design teams importing supplier geometry or reconstructing parts from scans.
Business hypothesis
A conversion service tied to recurring supplier/import workflows, then a specialized API if repeatable.
Possible advantage
A bridge between learned boundary completion and behavior-tested native histories could reduce remodeling while preserving important interfaces.
First test
Measure exact interface retention, useful editable coverage, subsequent revision success, and engineer cleanup time.
Reason to stop
Reject success criteria based only on watertight STEP output; stop if the supported editable subset is too small to save real work.

DualBrep, AutoBrep, and TransCAD cover complementary geometry and program representations. Their combination does not automatically recover the original design intent. DualBrep · AutoBrep · TransCAD

The research sequence to fund first

  1. Choose the paid problem and collect representative cases. Obtain a small licensed set of native designs, revisions and engineer acceptance criteria. Reproduce the current process and measure review time.
  2. Build the benchmark and a strong baseline. Freeze family-level splits and protected requirements before changing the model. Check evaluator failures by hand.
  3. Run the smallest useful adaptation. Compare an untrained small model, an adapted small model and a strong general-model agent under matched conditions. Include a template baseline.
  4. Test the central research claim. Hold initial geometry supervision constant, add revision behavior and preservation training, and measure whether future edits improve on new families.
  5. Buy data where the failures point. Acquire difficult references, richer operations and authentic revision sequences. Expand GPU spending only after data quality and evaluator reliability are demonstrated.
  6. Choose the company from the outcome. A reliable workflow can support a product even if model training adds little. A large, repeatable cost or acceptance advantage supports a specialist model business. A strong evaluator with weak generation may support validation infrastructure.

Stop or redirect if native data cannot be obtained on workable terms, if preserved requirements cannot be measured well enough, if the work is too infrequent to support repeat revenue, or if customer-specific setup overwhelms the saved engineering effort. Those are empirical decision points, not reasons to avoid the pilot.

The most promising experiment is not whether a model can generate a more attractive CAD screenshot. It is this: given equal geometry, tools and compute, does learning how designs respond to changes produce revisions that engineers accept faster?

The worked example

Your example: a NEMA 17 driver board in a cycloidal actuator

Keep the actuator as the demonstration and evaluation domain. It is cheap, it couples three domains, and a unit can be built in days. It is the proving ground for the product. The product itself is the environment plus the module library, and it treats vendor actuators and custom designs alike as packages with measured curves.

The market has moved under the example

Integrated brushless quasi-direct-drive actuators already serve the 5 to 20 N·m class. They pair 6:1 to 10:1 planetaries with dual absolute encoders, CAN and onboard field-oriented control.

A NEMA 17 stepper behind a printed 19:1 cycloid is a different device. It is position-controlled, slow and not backdrivable, which suits CNC axes and slow arm joints. Rev A's line that every robot arm and legged robot needs many of these modules is true of actuators and false of stepper modules.

The volumes are real for actuators. Figure says it built more than 9,000 actuators across more than 10 SKUs for about 350 robots by 29 April 2026. It designs them in-house for torque density and for DFM transitions from CNC to die-casting and stamping.232 Goldman Sachs' base case is 250,000 humanoids in 2030, which at 23 to 43 actuators each is 6 to 11 million units.233 Unitree's G1 starts at $13,500 with 23 degrees of freedom. The EDU version has up to 43.234

Who would buy it

OEM teams

In-house actuator teams such as Figure's. Their pain is family design, DFM transitions, supplier qualification and yield.232 They buy the family compiler, capability packs and check discrimination.

Labs

Labs customising sub-$200 printed actuators such as Berkeley Humanoid Lite's. Their pain is BOM, printed tolerance, thermal limits and durability.219 They buy capability packs, the tolerance stack, thermal-life checks and bench templates.

Integrators

The majority. K-Scale builds on RobStride, Primo chose 30 RobStride units for “one firmware, one debug tool, one set of spares,” and ToddlerBot runs on Dynamixel servos. Their pain is per-unit system identification, encoder calibration, CAN mapping, and integrating brackets, boards and firmware.223, 224 They buy the buy-versus-build advisor and vendor actuators packaged with measured curves.

For youIssue trackers rank the pain as sourcing and BOM first, printing tolerance and assembly second, encoder calibration third, CAN and firmware fourth and thermal fifth.236 Nobody on these forums asks for a tool that draws gears. The bet to test is that robot teams will pay for a tool that checks the integrated actuator before they order parts and measures it after.

The coupled design

Three facts shape the design before any agent starts. A NEMA 17 motor has a 42.3 mm square frame, four M3 holes on a 31 mm square, a 22 mm pilot and a 5 mm shaft. A cycloidal reducer whose ring has one more pin than the disc has lobes gives a ratio equal to the lobe count, and with the ring fixed the output turns opposite to the input. A closed-loop driver board commonly mounts on the back of the motor, with a magnetic encoder chip on the shaft axis facing a magnet on the rear shaft end.

One requirement at the output then reaches every domain.

The arithmetic, recomputed

Efficiency follows load. Dion et al. measured a machined, oil-lubricated 19:1 steel cycloid with 19 lobes and 20 pins, the same proportions as this design at about a quarter of the scale. Efficiency was 0.54 at 7% of rated load and 0.89 at full load.203 A wire-EDM steel 10:1 robot actuator peaked at 82.3% from electrical input to mechanical output.204 A constrained-drive bench averaged 61% to 63%.205 Printed PLA units behind NEMA 17 steppers measured 60% to 66%, with 60 to 150 arcmin of backlash, and failed after about two hours.206 At 5 N·m the reducer runs at about half of an assumed 10 N·m rating. A curve fitted to Dion's two steel points gives about 0.85 there, and the printed units above measured 60% to 66%. Plan at 0.60 to 0.70 until it is measured. This example uses 0.65.

Torque falls with speed. The Pololu SY42STH47-1206A datasheet plots a 24 V, 1.2 A, half-step pull-out curve. It reads 45.0 N·cm at 200 pulses per second, then 40.1 at 1,500, 34.0 at 2,000, 25.0 at 3,000, 20.0 at 4,000 and 13.9 at 5,000. At 400 half-steps per revolution those points span 30 to 750 rpm. Torque at 600 rpm is 44% of the 30 rpm value, and interpolation gives about 21 N·cm at 570 rpm.207 Rev A gave no source for its motor figures. This datasheet now supplies the roll-off.

The sheet also prints a holding torque of 31.1 N·cm, which is below its own low-speed pull-out. That cannot be right. The curve's 45 equals Pololu's 44 oz·in holding figure, so the axis is very plausibly oz·in with the wrong label.208 On that reading the real torque is about 0.71 of the printed values, roughly 14 N·cm at 600 rpm. Continuous duty is bounded by rated current and heat. A comparable StepperOnline motor specifies an 80 K rise at rated current with two phases on and Class B insulation at 130 °C.209

The design misses by about 2x to 2.7x. The motor must deliver 5 / (19 × 0.65) = 0.405 N·m. The board's 1.5 A limit scales a 0.45 N·m, 1.68 A motor to about 0.40 N·m even at standstill. At 570 rpm on 24 V the curve gives about 0.21 N·m as an upper bound, and the toy model below uses 0.208. On the oz·in reading it gives about 0.15 N·m. REQ-01 fails at speed on 24 V. The fixes are a 36 to 48 V bus, a higher ratio with a slower output, or a larger motor. In the toy model below, 36 V closes part of the gap. 48 V closes it for ratios from 20:1 to 29:1, and above that the ring pins run out of room.

This is the coupled failure the product should report before a person computes it. An agent in SolidWorks and KiCad learns none of it unless it thinks to compute it.

Move the ratio and the bus voltage

This is a toy version of the requirement table the product would show. Every constant is listed under the table. A real build would take them from the motor's package, the reducer's measured curve and the board's design.

Toy-model assumptions, every constant the table uses:

  • Requirement: 5.00 N·m continuous at 30 rpm at the output.
  • Reducer efficiency η = 0.717 × f / (f + 0.0513), where f is output torque over an assumed 10 N·m reducer rating, so f = 0.5 and η = 0.650. The curve has the shape of Dion et al.'s steel cycloid fitted to 0.54 at 7% load and 0.89 at full load, scaled by 0.766 to the printed planning value.
  • Motor: Rev A's assumed 0.45 N·m low-speed torque at 1.68 A per phase, with torque proportional to current. Only the shape of the roll-off comes from the 1.2 A Pololu part.
  • Torque available at motor speed n on bus voltage V is 0.45 × min(1, 264 × V / 24 / n) N·m. The 264 rpm corner speed at 24 V makes torque at 600 rpm 44% of the low-speed value, as on the datasheet curve. Corner speed scales linearly with bus voltage. This is an upper bound.
  • Board current limit 1.50 A per phase. Phase current needed is 1.68 A × motor torque needed / 0.45 N·m.
  • Encoder 12 bits, 4,096 counts per motor revolution. Output resolution is 360° / 4,096 / ratio.
  • Ring pins 4 mm in diameter on a 48 mm pitch circle, one more pin than the disc has lobes. Material between pins is 48 × sin(180° / pins) − 4 mm.

On 24 V no ratio passes, because above the corner speed a stepper delivers roughly constant power. A higher ratio raises motor speed as fast as it cuts the torque needed, so REQ-01 stays at 2.57 N·m from 9:1 upward. 36 V lifts it to 3.86 N·m from 14:1. 48 V lifts it to 5.15 N·m from 18:1. All four requirements pass on 48 V from 20:1 to 29:1, where the board's current limit is met and the ring pins still have room. That is the result an agent should report, and it is a better demonstration than a toy that passes.

The encoder is four requirements

A 12-bit encoder gives 0.088° per count, which is 4.4 electrical degrees on a 50-pole-pair stepper. Raw magnetic encoders carry ±0.8° to ±1° of integral non-linearity, which is up to ±50 electrical degrees of commutation error before calibration. Every working closed-loop stepper board calibrates against the motor's own 200 full steps and stores a table, and Mechaduino reaches about ±0.1° worst case after its routine.210 So the single resolution figure splits into four checks.

RequirementCheckAS5600, I²CAS5047D/P, SPI, from the AS5047D datasheetMA732, SPI
BitsCounts per output revolution meet the output resolution12 bits14 bits9 to 14 bits, set by the filter window
Accuracy after calibrationError against the motor's 200 full steps after the stored table±1° raw±0.8° raw, about ±0.1° after calibration0.7° raw at 25 °C, 1.1° over temperature
LatencyDelay fits the commutation budget at 570 rpmFails. SimpleFOC flags the part as unreliable.Passes. The core delay for SPI reads is 90 to 110 µs, and the chip's dynamic angle error compensation corrects for it. ABI and UVW outputs lag 1.5 to 1.9 µs after compensation.Passes, 8 to 10 µs
Sample rateSustains the control loop, 6.5 kHz on MechaduinoFails for field-oriented control over I²CPassesPasses

Sources: AS5600, AS5047D, MA732 and Mechaduino documents, SimpleFOC's sensor notes.210, 211, 212, 213, 214 moteus already models the firmware side of this contract. Its Apache-licensed configuration has rotor_to_output_ratio as a first-class parameter, fault_temperature and temperature_margin for board and motor, and power limits that scale with PWM rate.215

Tolerance and life

  • Corners decide stress. In simulation a single 0.8 mm roller error, 27% of the roller radius, raised peak von Mises stress about 15x while input torque changed 3%.216 A stress check on nominal geometry passes designs that fail at their tolerance corners.
  • Printed play grows. Roozing's PLA units showed 0.20° to 0.35° of play fresh, stiffness of 633 to 1,468 N·m/rad and about 90% efficiency. Play roughly doubled after a 10-hour endurance block as elephant's-foot deviations wore off.217
  • Heat breaks polymer discs. A PA12-CF15 disc printed by FDM survived 48 minutes, 95,040 cycles, at 32 N·m and 2,000 rpm. It failed by thermally accelerated fatigue at the bearing seat, although nominal FEM showed 2.5 MPa against ample strength. PA12's glass transition at 40 to 50 °C sits below the operating temperature.220 A polymer reducer needs a disc-temperature bound and a run-in and wear protocol.
  • Fits come from the process. As-printed nylon is IT13 to IT14, quick-turn CNC IT9 to IT10 and a reamed hole IT6 to IT7. An H7 bearing seat, a 30 µm span at 50 to 80 mm, is out of reach for any printed part and compiles to “insert or post-machine.”240, 241
  • Tolerance is a vendor-tier variable. Nylon powder-bed tolerance is ±0.3 mm at JLC3DP. At Xometry it is ±1.40 mm in the unreviewed prototype tier for 50 to 80 mm parts and ±0.25 mm in XY and ±0.42 mm in Z after engineer review. Quick-turn CNC holds ±0.05 to 0.13 mm.237, 238, 239
  • Hardware reuse sets iteration cost. Builds take 1 to 3 days. A printed reducer's bill of materials is dominated by bearings and shoulder screws, €60 to €90 of a €65 to €133 total, against €6 of filament.218, 221

The joint in each prototype

The same robot joint, seen three ways

Every piece of this work returns to one robot-arm joint: a NEMA 17 motor, a reducer and a driver board. Datum uses it as its flagship check, Meridian walks through it as a project, and the research report uses it to test the engineering-change company. Each treatment shows a different part of the problem.

Datum: a joint that would have stalled, caught at the spec sheet

The flagship is a robot-arm joint: a NEMA 17 stepper, a printed cycloidal reducer, a driver board on the back of the motor. Holding 0.5 kg at 400 mm on a 0.3 kg link takes 2.55 N·m. With a safety factor of 2 the drivetrain has to deliver a margin of at least 2.

At the assumed 65% reducer efficiency the margin is 2.29, and a plain calculation would pass it. But nobody has measured that efficiency; one hobby test is the only data. Across a plausible band of 50% to 80% the margin runs from 1.76 to 2.82. Datum fails the check and names the assumption that decides it.

Checks, with the failing check open

The interface, on fixture data. It states the same margin against the safety-factored requirement, so it reads 1.15 with a band of 0.97 to 1.41. The figures in the text above are the ones the check engine's tests assert. The flagship project that would produce this report from real design code is not built yet.

Meridian: the joint as a chain of decisions

"Build a robotic arm" becomes a chain of decisions. The project needs reach, payload, speed, precision, motion limits, available components, manufacturing access and a budget. A single joint is a useful first scope because its interfaces and acceptance criteria can be made explicit.

  1. Establish the purchased motor. Select the exact NEMA 17 motor and attach its drawing or source. A frame designation alone does not determine the shaft, body length, torque curve, current or connector. The reference project contains illustrative assumptions that still need confirmation.
  2. Define the mechanical interface. Represent the shaft and coupling, mounting pattern, bearing arrangement and drive housing with named dimensions and datums. Choose a reduction ratio and manufacturing process. Generate actual solids and check the included bodies and sampled poses.
  3. Choose the electronics arrangement. A driver beside the motor and a remote driver imply different power, signal, wiring and heat constraints. Record the decision and component sources. Model the board, pads, nets, copper and declared body heights, and do not infer electrical suitability from appearance.
  4. Place the board in the assembly. Save its 3D position and rotation. Shared substrate, drills and component envelopes let the mechanical checks evaluate the declared placement. Unmodeled cables, screw-head access and purchased-part details remain explicit review items.
  5. Verify the intended behavior and handoff. Run assembly checks and native PCB DRC. If the controller includes RTL, compile it and run an appropriate testbench separately. Inspect the revision, scope and assumptions of each result before exporting a review bundle.

What about a synthetic muscle? The same requirements-and-evidence process would start with measured force against contraction, pressure and flow, geometry, hysteresis, temperature and cycle life. A predictive design needs a calibrated material and actuator model and physical experiments. Meridian's release does not implement synthetic-muscle constitutive or fluid models, and the agent cannot fill that gap with an invented simulation result.

The research report: replacing the motor in an existing joint

Consider a customer replacing a motor in an existing joint. "NEMA 17" alone is insufficient to determine the exact shaft, mounting details, torque, driver, thermal behavior or connector. The system should use the selected component's actual drawing and requirements, and it should identify missing dimensions before generating an apparently precise adapter.

The first model predicts the mechanical revision: mounting geometry, shaft coupling or gearbox interface, relevant clearances and a bounded feature patch. The checks rebuild the assembly, measure protected interfaces, examine the specified motion and flag assumptions. A separate electrical workflow handles the chosen driver, connections and board constraints. Shared connector locations, mounting features, cable space and heat-related requirements connect the two.

The training record is more than the final adapter. It includes which reference was mistaken, which variant collided, what the engineer preserved, why a proposed simplification was rejected and which tests were necessary. With permission to learn from those cases, the company accumulates evidence about successful changes within that class of product.

A hypothetical paid pilot would compare ten or more historical substitutions against the customer's existing process, then attempt new revisions with the engineer reviewing them. The number is a starting proposal, not statistical sufficiency. The deliverable is a reviewable revision package. Physical acceptance still depends on the task's real manufacturing and test process, and CAD validity alone does not establish hardware performance.

revision service→repeatable family workflow→learned revision model→broader subsystem changes

That path from a feature to a company also creates a natural reason to add PCB and testing capabilities once customers repeatedly need them.

The worked example

What the repo looks like

Everything is text under version control, so an agent edits it with tools it already knows and a reviewer reads a diff. Start on open tools the models have seen. Use build123d for geometry, KiCad files with kicad-cli for boards, Zener or atopile for circuits after a license and roadmap check, and a normal firmware toolchain. Export STEP, KiCad files and Gerbers so nobody feels locked in. Do not write a geometry kernel.

Rev B adds six things to the Rev A layout. Ports and mates are typed. Contracts span domains. Capability packs and compiled rules describe what each vendor can make and what each standard demands. A bench directory holds plans and predicted-against-measured records. The build writes a provenance manifest. The toolchain is pinned and hashed.

Layout for the actuator
actuator-n17/
├─ requirements/
│  ├─ actuator.toml        # REQ-01 to REQ-12: unit, limit, check and bench step for each
│  └─ sources.toml         # dated requirement sources: IEC 61800-5-1, EU PLD, vendor tiers
├─ ports/
│  ├─ motor_mount.py       # NEMA 17 face, bolt square, pilot, shaft axis, typed mates
│  ├─ encoder.py           # air gap, bits, accuracy after calibration, latency, sample rate
│  ├─ power_data.py        # connector, pinout, bus range 24 to 48 V
│  └─ regmap.toml          # registers shared by firmware and host tools
├─ contracts/
│  └─ actuator.py          # assume-guarantee contracts across motor, reducer, board, firmware
├─ mech/
│  ├─ reducer.py           # disc profile, ring pins, eccentric, output pins
│  └─ housing.py
├─ elec/
│  ├─ driver.zen           # schematic as code
│  ├─ board.py             # outline, holes, keep-outs derived from ports
│  └─ layout.kicad_pcb     # routed board
├─ fw/
│  ├─ src/                 # control loop, comms
│  ├─ generated/           # constants written by the build
│  └─ sim/                 # 2-phase stepper plant, written in-house
├─ packs/                  # capability packs: vendor, process, tier, tolerance, source, date
│  ├─ jlc3dp-mjf-pa12.toml
│  ├─ xometry-mjf-proto.toml
│  └─ jlccnc-al6061.toml
├─ rules/                  # standards as data, each value with its clause
│  ├─ ipc2221b.toml
│  └─ iec60664.toml
├─ checks/                 # read-only to builders, mounted only in the judge sandbox
│  ├─ t0_static/  t1_geometry/  t2_physics/  t3_long/
│  └─ mutants/             # planted faults every check must catch
├─ bench/
│  ├─ plans/               # generated bring-up, run-in and endurance plans
│  └─ runs/                # predicted against measured, hashed to firmware and script
├─ toolchain.lock          # container digests, tool versions, generator hashes
├─ packages.lock           # pinned modules with license class
├─ DECISIONS.md            # why 20:1 on 48 V, what was tried, what failed
└─ build/
   ├─ manifest.json        # every artifact hashed, every done claim linked to evidence
   ├─ rules/actuator.kicad_dru   # compiled from rules/ and packs/
   └─ step/  gerbers/  bom/  firmware/  report/
Typed ports and a mate resolved in closed form
# ports/motor_mount.py: defined once, used by every domain
NEMA17 = MotorMount(frame=42.3*mm, bolt_square=31*mm, bolt="M3",
                    pilot=22*mm, shaft=5*mm)
pilot = Port("motor.pilot", kind="cylindrical_fit", axis=NEMA17.shaft_axis,
             fit="H7/g6", cite="ISO 286-2")

# mech/housing.py: the mate is solved, never placed from a render
housing.mate(pilot, kind="concentric_planar")

# elec/board.py: board geometry is derived, never typed in
board.outline = square(NEMA17.frame)
board.holes   = bolt_pattern(NEMA17.bolt_square, clearance_for=NEMA17.bolt)
board.place(encoder_ic, at=NEMA17.shaft_axis)

# fw/generated/constants.h: written by the build
#define COUNTS_PER_OUTPUT_REV  (4096 * 20)   /* encoder.cpr * reducer.ratio */
#define OUTPUT_DIR             (-1)          /* fixed ring: output reverses */
A requirement with its bench step, and the result its check returns
[REQ-01]
text   = "Output torque available at 30 rpm"
min    = "5.00 N*m"
check  = "t2_physics/motor_torque_speed_voltage"
inputs = ["motor.curve", "reducer.efficiency", "board.bus_voltage", "board.i_limit"]
bench  = "bench/plans/torque_speed.yaml"    # measures the same quantity
signed = "compile step reviewed by a person, 2026-10-04"

# result at 19:1 on 24 V, written for an agent to act on
{"req": "REQ-01", "pass": false, "value": "2.57 N*m", "limit": ">= 5.00 N*m",
 "margin": "-48.5%", "binding": "motor torque at 570 rpm on 24 V",
 "where": "motor.curve above its 264 rpm corner speed",
 "fixes": ["bus 48 V with ratio 20 to 29", "lower output speed", "larger motor"],
 "artifact": "build/checks/REQ-01/curve.svg", "toolchain": "sha256:41ab..."}
A capability pack, and the fit check it drives

vendor  = "Xometry"
process = "HP Multi Jet Fusion, PA12"
tier    = "prototype, no engineer review"
source  = "https://www.xometry.com/capabilities/3d-printing-service/hp-multi-jet-fusion/"
read_on = "2026-10-03"
[tolerance]
"50-80 mm" = "+/-1.40 mm"
it_grade   = "IT13-14"

# result of t0_static/process_fit on the pilot port
{"req": "FIT-03", "pass": false, "value": "IT13 as printed", "limit": "H7, 30 um span",
 "fixes": ["press-fit steel insert", "post-machine the bore"],
 "pack": "xometry-mjf-proto.toml@2026-10-03"}
An example bench record, with illustrative values
{"run": "bench/runs/unit03-torque-speed.json", "plan": "torque_speed.yaml",
 "firmware": "sha256:...", "script": "sha256:...", "instruments": "read-only",
 "actuation": "granted for this plan only",
 "predicted": {"REQ-01": "5.15 N*m"}, "measured": {"REQ-01": "measured value here"},
 "comparable": true, "writes_back": "registry/nema17-cyc20@0.3.1/curve"}

The result names the binding quantity, where it binds and the fixes, so the agent can act without a second investigation. Every artifact carries a hash, so a done claim points at evidence, which is the Agentrys rule.176 The toolchain lock pins container digests, tool versions and generator hashes. A changed generator invalidates the releases built with it, and repeated runs catch nondeterminism. Mouro, a vendor, reports that on identical input Freerouting with four threads produced about 20 DRC errors where one thread produced none.168 LibreLane already runs the open chip flow in a Nix-pinned environment.190 Every tool also offers a mock tier that checks a request before the real run, as Zoo's MCP server does.124

The worked example

The same change in both setups

The fair comparison is a coding agent on Fusion Compute MCP and a KiCad MCP server, the strongest stock setup available today. Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code already scored 0.750 on CAD Arena's 18 parts on 25 September and 75.0 on EEBench's 13 circuit tasks on 29 September.74, 76 Use this setup for single parts and simple boards. The difference shows when one change has to stay consistent across domains, and when the data behind each part has to agree with itself.

Changing the reducer from 19:1 to 25:1 on 24 V

On stock tools the change takes separate edits in Fusion, KiCad and the firmware, and nothing flags a stale firmware constant. In the environment it takes one edit, and the result names the bus voltage as the binding input.

Coding agent on Fusion MCP and KiCad MCPInside the environment
What the agent editsDisc profile, ring pins and housing through Fusion TypeScript. Current limit in the KiCad schematic. Scaling and direction constants in firmware. Each one separately, each one from context.One parameter, the reducer ratio.
What catches a missed editFusion's kernel catches invalid geometry. Nothing catches a firmware constant that no longer matches the ratio.The build regenerates pin count, housing and firmware constants, then re-runs every check that depends on them.
What it learns about torque at speedOnly what it thinks to calculate.REQ-02 now passes at 1.15 A. REQ-01 still fails at 2.57 N·m, because above the corner speed a higher ratio buys no torque at 30 rpm. The result names the bus voltage as the binding input.
Data consistencyA footprint, symbol or BOM line can drift from its part number while DRC still reports zero errors, as JLCPCB's 50 mismatches showed.82T0 compares the part number, symbol, footprint, 3D body and BOM line of every component before any slower check runs.
What a reviewer seesA cloud document history, a board file diff and a screenshot.A text diff, a visual diff and a requirement table with one change of state.
Trying four ratios at onceFusion's beta allows two concurrent sessions per user, each capped at an hour.91Four worktrees, four headless builds, one comparison table.

How Datum works, from the 3 October design notes

One graph, checked on every change

Any agent can generate a design. Datum is where it becomes trustworthy. Datum is the contract and evidence layer for machines that move. It records the interfaces between mechanics, electronics, wiring and firmware as typed contracts, checks them with deterministic tools that state their assumptions, and ties bench results to requirements. Codex, Claude Code and Datum's own agent are all clients of it.

Where it stands: the research, the design and nine packages are done, with 991 tests passing. The layer that joins them into a running product is designed and not yet built. What exists has the detail.

This section describes the design; What exists says how much of it is built. A design is TypeScript that executes into a typed graph: parts, the ports they expose, the mates and connections between ports, requirements, and parameters that each record where their value came from. Geometry can be modeled in Datum, taken from the catalog, or imported from any CAD tool. The contracts and the checks are the same in each case.

  1. Intake. A spec sheet, not an open chat: payload, reach, speed, supply, process, budget. Each field is tagged as stated, assumed or default.
  2. Contract first. Requirements bind to checks before any geometry exists. Interfaces and joints are declared before parts are shaped.
  3. Design on a proposal. The agent edits a working copy. Every write rebuilds the design and re-runs the cheap checks.
  4. Review like a pull request. What changed, the check results, the assumptions, and what was not checked.
  5. Accept. The proposal becomes an immutable version with its evidence.
  6. Bench. A measurement moves a requirement from checked to bench-confirmed, or overturns the assumption it contradicts.

Meridian, the earlier local prototype, stores the same idea differently. Its canonical project lives in SQLite as revisioned design records with requirements, memory, jobs and evidence, and its domain engines are CadQuery on OpenCascade, KiCad, slang, Icarus and Yosys. Meridian describes that shared project.

Architecture

Harness design

The harness is the loop, the tools and the checks around the model. The picture comes first, then the rules behind it. Rev B changes two things in the picture. The judge now runs in three stages, with deterministic checks deciding, and the physical loop now writes into a module registry that feeds the next design.

Deterministic first, LLM advisory, human final

Most of the judge can be deterministic. Kernel queries cover clearance, interference and mass. Electrical and design rules, circuit simulation at tolerance corners, finite element and thermal analysis cover the rest, and the data-consistency tier runs before all of them. An LLM reviewer reads what those cannot measure, such as whether a connector can be reached by hand or whether a test really tests its requirement. It can flag a design and cannot pass one, because “a mechanical rejection overrides an LLM approval, never the reverse.”24 A person signs off. Anthropic found a separate evaluator tuned to be skeptical far more tractable than a builder made critical of its own work, and it still took several rounds of tuning.1

Builders cannot read or write the checks

The check tree and solver outputs are read-only to builders at the filesystem and API level, and the hidden tolerances are not mounted at all. The final verdict runs in a hermetic sandbox from a clean checkout. In PROCTOR's test, agents scored 100% on 47 tasks by reading cached answer keys and 68.1% once sandboxed.24 Canary tasks that must fail run in every batch. Impossible tasks, whose requirements contradict each other, report each model's cheating rate.19, 25

Give agents a way to say the spec is wrong

An escalate_spec_conflict tool pauses the task and returns “queued for human review.” A tool like it cut hacking from 23.6% to 5.3% with no loss of solve rate.23 Remove every prompt line that asks the model not to cheat. METR found such instructions had “a nearly negligible effect.”21

Test the checks

Every check is mutation-tested, and each module publishes a check-discrimination score, the share of planted faults its checks catch. The planted faults include a bolt circle off by one hole, a trace one width class too thin, a ratio constant scaled wrong and a footprint swapped for its neighbour, and they run on every model release. CADTests refined its tests until the mutation score passed 90%. SWE-ABS shows what weak suites cost, with 19.78% of solved patches failing once tests were strengthened.26, 43 Lyon's failure case is a ready-made mutant.151

Agree what done means, with a person on the compile step

A planner expands the prompt into requirements, each with a unit, a limit, a check and a bench step. A person reviews and signs that compile step, which is the cheapest place to spend human attention. Anthropic's harness had the same step, a contract agreed between builder and evaluator before each chunk of work, because the spec alone was too high-level to test.1 The compiler refuses requirements without a measurable acceptance test and asks every clarifying question at once before building. Builders cannot change a limit or a check. Changing one takes a waiver that a person signs.

Thin loop, rich environment, redefined

Rich now means rich in verifiers, state, typed references and error messages that localise the fault by naming the margin, the selector, the net or the variable that changed. Thin means few hand-written CAD-operation wrappers. Anthropic's guidance is to build on general tools the model already knows and to keep asking what scaffolding can come out.2 In one Anthropic example, writing code against tools instead of passing every result through context cut a workflow from 150,000 tokens to 2,000.4 ComAct found that retrieval over thousands of raw API documents made results worse.47

Ship knowledge as executable interfaces

Prose skills are unreliable. In the chip-flow study they cut Claude Code's physical-implementation completion from 7 of 8 to 3 of 8 while cutting its Tcl errors.170 WebDev-Skills-Bench found that skill injection lowered mean Pass@2 by 1.3 to 4.2 points and raised token cost by 72% to 394%.10 IoT-SkillsBench found that expert-written skills lifted firmware pass@1 from 101 of 126 to 124 of 126, while LLM-written skills lowered it to 95 of 126.12 SIGIL measured 26.2% to 54.0% adherence to a SKILL.md file, against up to 100% when the skill was compiled into an executable harness.11 ORFS-agent's retrieval helped at 200 iterations and hurt at 600.13 Module knowledge therefore ships as version-pinned code with tests, and any generated documentation is gated on hardware validation.

Give every tool an operational contract

Each tool declares what is loaded, which actions are valid next and what its result looks like. Sessions carry instance and request IDs. The server enforces the split between query and exec, as OpenROAD-MCP does by rejecting mutating commands on its query tool.8 Cost per verified milestone is a standing metric. Deng et al.'s typed harness cut tool-state errors from 31.7% of events to none, on one design with one run per configuration.170

The model states constraints and solvers place things

The agent says that the encoder chip sits on the shaft axis and the connector faces the housing slot. A constraint solver, a parametric generator or a router produces the coordinates. Cycloid profiles come from equations. Motor, driver, reducer and encoder selection becomes a constraint problem over a typed catalogue, which the model writes and a solver solves.63 Placement and routing come from solvers. Use your own, run GPL Freerouting as a subprocess, or exchange files with Quilter.73, 266

Keep an archive of elites

Iteration does not improve steadily. Anthropic's author often preferred a middle iteration to the last, and the physics-in-the-loop team saw results destabilise as iterations piled up.1, 39 Keep the best design in each niche, for torque density, cost, thermal margin and part count, with every metric kept separate. Gate candidates by admission, then correctness, then feasibility, then performance.14 Selection matters as much as generation. CodeMonkeys recovered half the gap between 45.8% and 69.8% by selecting better.15

Cheap checks first, slow checks in the background, nothing twice

Order the checks by cost and stop at the first failing tier. Cross-domain references form a dependency graph, so a change invalidates only the checks downstream of it. Pre-solve gates for units, empty selectors, trivial displacement and job submission save whole solver runs. CADEngBench found that 573 of 1,809 FEA attempts failed before the solver ran.42 Slow jobs run in the background and the agent resumes when results land. State lives in the repo, with a decision log, the requirement status table and a commit per agent step, which is how Anthropic's long-running harnesses hand over between context windows.3

A person approves what cannot be undone

Placing an order, releasing a revision, waiving a requirement and granting bench actuation go through dedicated tools that wait for a person. Everything else runs unattended. Anthropic gives the same advice. An action gets its own tool when it needs a confirmation, a security boundary or an audit trail.2

Measure the harness and delete what stops helping

Run the held-out eval on every model release, with and without each harness component. Measure pass^k as well as pass^1. Report an audited false-done rate with its denominator, and the judge's false-alarm and miss rates against human adjudication. Count cost per verified pass. Repeat runs, because one run per configuration is the norm in this field. The chip-flow paper's headline moved from 105.92x to 141.2x within three days.34, 170 Anthropic removed its sprint structure when a stronger model no longer needed it. Its full harness took six hours and $200 against 20 minutes and $9 for a single agent.1

What each component assumes

Two components never come out. They are the checks kept out of the builder's reach and the physics checks with the bench. Every other component is a bet about a model limitation, re-tested at each model release or tool change.

The same rules in Datum: the gates live in the environment, not in the prompt

By design, the same rules bind Datum's agent and an outside agent connected over MCP, because the tool host enforces them and the prompt does not have to. An agent that ignores its instructions still cannot do the things below. The harness and the working rules exist; the tool host that enforces these gates is not built yet.

If an agent tries toThe environment
Advance past a failed buildKeeps the last good design and returns the errors with file and line.
Skip re-checking after a changeRuns the cheap check tiers on every write.
Submit over failing blockersRefuses, unless each is waived with a reason the reviewer will see.
Cite a catalog or standard value that does not existRecords it as an assumption.
Report a requirement as metComputes the status itself from check results and measurements.
Change the main designRoutes every change into a proposal that a person accepts or rejects.

What the evidence says matters, in order

  • A deterministic gate. Without it, valid designs fell from 100% to 0%.
  • Interfaces declared before geometry. Success rose from 89.2% to 100%.
  • Persistent, localized repair state. Recovery 0.92 with it, 0.49 without.
  • Images. Helpful, expensive, and the least sufficient: four of nine successful repairs in one study were invisible in any render.

Agents never emit coordinates or copper

Mates place parts. The autorouter routes. Synthesis maps logic. Every language model scored 0.00 on larger boards when asked to route directly, and an agent stopped inventing rotation angles once it was given a tool that says "lay this face on the bed".

The agent works on intent. Solvers do geometry.

Thirteen working rules, each with a reason

Every rule encodes something the model cannot yet do alone. On each model release the eval runs with a rule removed; if the score holds, the rule is deleted.

Read the project before you act

Start from the digest: requirements, parts, failing checks, open assumptions, recent decisions.

Persistent state was worth about half of recovery performance in one study.

Ask once, with defaults

One spec sheet of questions. Every question has a default and a reason it matters.

Agents fail by silently committing to a plausible framing, and cannot tell reliably when to ask. A default makes every question safe to skip.

Contract first, geometry second

Requirements, parameters, components, ports, mates, drivetrain and load case come before any shape.

A torque budget that fails is cheapest to find before a housing exists.

Propose a plan

Steps tied to requirement ids, with the assumptions being made.

An explicit plan stage was worth 3.7 points of validity in one system.

Small steps, and read the result of each

One part or feature at a time. Fix a failed build before anything else.

A failed operation that silently advances state is how agents lose holes and produce disconnected solids.

Never compute a coordinate

Mates, patterns, face-relative positions, measure tools.

Frontier models score near chance on hard 3D rotation tasks.

Every number has a source

User, catalog, standard, datasheet, computed, or assumption. No source means assumption, with a band where a margin depends on it.

Blocking ungrounded parameters cut that class of error from 44.3% to 2.1% in one study.

Use the catalog and the generators

Motors, bearings, fasteners and the cycloidal profile exist already.

Models handle sketch-and-extrude and fail on sweeps, lofts and the relations inside gears.

Fix a failure at its cause

Change the design. Never weaken a check, and never waive a blocker to get finished.

Improving one requirement can break another, so every fix is followed by a full re-check.

Look when looking helps

A marked view or a section to confirm which face is meant. Not after every step.

Marks raised visual grounding from 25.7% to 86.4%.

Write things down as you go

Decisions with the alternatives rejected, lessons, sourced facts.

Durable state belongs in files, not in context.

Before you submit

Run every tier, ask for an independent check, read every warning, then summarize what changed, what was checked, what was not, and what is assumed.

Self-evaluation is lenient.

Say what is true

Never "verified". Say what was checked, under which assumptions, and what was not.

A requirement is confirmed only by a measurement on real hardware.

The harness inside Meridian, from the 1 October field guide

Engineering state is authoritative. Model output is a proposal.

The harness is the machinery around the model: what it can observe, which actions it can request, how changes are validated, which checks must follow, and how unfinished work recovers. In Meridian the runtime has one coordinator. Mechanics and electronics specialist reviews are deterministic evidence summaries, not independent model experts.

  1. Observe Read state. Inspect the saved design, its revision, relevant memory and current evidence.
  2. Act Request a typed tool. Use named actions with strict arguments and stable domain references.
  3. Verify Execute the engine. Obtain actual geometry, DRC, compilation or workflow results.
  4. Reconcile Check current state. Persist scoped evidence, then inspect conflicts and outstanding verification.

Canonical data, rather than executable CAD prompts

The design describes bounded features, arithmetic expressions, datums and mates. Parameter expressions use a restricted arithmetic AST interpreter. An agent cannot submit arbitrary Python, a shell command, an executable path, an unrestricted file path or an arbitrary URL through a model tool. The shared registry exposes 19 typed tools to the coordinator and to MCP.

Native adapters choose fixed commands and constrain time, memory and output. They return unknown for unavailable, interrupted or malformed execution. These are concrete boundaries. They do not constitute a universal filesystem sandbox for arbitrary native software.

Revision protection

A design edit includes expectedRevision. SQLite checks it in a transaction before saving. If the user changes R6 to R7 while an agent is preparing an R6 edit, the stale edit is rejected, and the agent must inspect the new state instead of overwriting the user's work.

Evidence remains attached to its captured revision. Restoring an old design creates a new revision, preserving history and making earlier results stale. Same-revision checks merge without wiping unrelated current evidence.

Explore the revision rule

Illustration only. These buttons do not run Meridian or an engineering engine.

State example
Project revisionR6
Check revisionR6

An illustrative check evaluates R6. Its result is current for R6 and only covers that check's declared scope.

Verification is an obligation after an edit

The coordinator enforces checks even if the model ends its response immediately after saving a change. One policy is shared by live execution, job events and recovery. Obligations survive cancellation, budgets and trace truncation.

Successful editRequired toolScope
update_parameters
edit_design
edit_specification		run_checksApplicable assembly and project checks.
set_board_placementrun_checksChanged assembly placement. Unchanged copper creates no new native-layout obligation.
edit_electronicsrun_checks and check_electronicsAssembly and local checks, and native KiCad DRC.
update_logiccheck_logicslang language compilation. Simulation and synthesis are separate, explicit workflow actions.

Required tools must supply evidence for the final current revision. If a user edits after a check, that result cannot establish verification for the newer revision. verifiedRevisions and pendingVerification keep this distinction visible.

Pass

The evaluated criterion passed within its scope.

Warn

Execution has findings or a coverage limitation to review.

Fail

An evaluated condition or assertion failed.

Unknown

Evidence is absent, unavailable or incomplete.

Stale

The result belongs to an earlier project revision.

A completed job is an execution state. It may truthfully finish with failing DRC or unknown strength. It does not approve the design. Fabrication manifests retain findings and explicitly record manufacturingApproved: false.

Durable jobs, bounded attempts

SQLite stores intent before execution and appends ordered action and result events as the job proceeds, so the interface can show progress without waiting for the entire run. The local scheduler supports two concurrent projects, one active coordinator per project and at most 100 outstanding jobs. It expects one API process.

queued→running→completedorstopped
failedcancelledinterruptedbudget_reached→ resume as a new linked attempt
8
provider rounds per attempt
16
tool actions per attempt, invalid calls included
120 s
elapsed-time budget per attempt
35 s
maximum provider request timeout

Requests are constrained by remaining time, observations are capped at 20,000 characters with explicit truncation, and three identical failed calls stop execution. Native work has its own limits. Budget checks and cooperative cancellation occur at action boundaries, so these numbers are not instantaneous kill guarantees.

Cancel without pretending nothing happened

A queued job can be cancelled before tools run. For a running job, cancellation is requested and takes effect at a checkpoint. An already committed edit remains saved. In-flight native work or a remote provider may continue until its action returns, and unfinished required checks remain pending.

Resume from authoritative state

On startup, lost running jobs become interrupted. Failed, cancelled, interrupted or budget-limited attempts can be resumed, and a completed job cannot. Resume creates a new linked job with a fresh attempt budget. It rereads the current project and uses bounded prior observations as untrusted context. Pending checks are carried separately so truncation cannot erase them.

Recovery also compares saved revisions to detect a change committed just before its event was lost. The local parser does not replay additive commands such as "add box" or "save memory". It inspects saved state and runs outstanding checks. A connected model can plan further work from current state and prior evidence.

Memory records intent. Evidence records evaluation.

Project memory contains decisions, requirements, measurements and notes with revision context. Retrieval is explicit bounded text search. There is no hidden vector service, and a remembered measurement does not become verified engineering evidence.

Requirements carry targets, assumptions, verification methods and links to results. Each check retains method, scope, metrics and revision. An agent trace records observable arguments, results and summaries, not private reasoning. Project text and tool outputs are untrusted data, and they cannot grant additional tool authority.

Physical tests have a separate provenance boundary

A user can record a procedure, observation, result and source, operator or report. No agent or MCP tool can fabricate a physical test. Records identify themselves as human-reported and independentlyVerified: false.

Linking that report to selected requirements changes the specification, so a revision-protected transaction advances the project revision and stales earlier evidence. testedRevision preserves the captured revision. An unlinked report is a same-revision annotation. Analysis-only checks cannot discharge a physical-test requirement.

Three connection modes

ModeWhat executesConnection
Local toolsA small deterministic command parser. No language model runs.Offline.
OpenAIResponses function tools with explicit history.User API key, with separate API billing.
ChatGPT subscriptionPublished local-app sign-in and inference integration.User-initiated authorization and eligible account models.

API keys entered in Settings stay in backend memory for that process. The app does not reuse Codex credentials. Windows protects persisted sign-in refresh tokens with DPAPI, and other systems keep credentials in server memory. Real-account authorization and paid inference have not been validated.

What the papers contributed

These primary papers informed the harness design. Their experiments concern other tasks and do not establish Meridian's design quality. The product consequences are implementation inferences.

Yang et al. · 2024 · v3

SWE-agent

Interfaces matter. Its study of agent-computer interfaces informed named actions, concise engine feedback and editing guardrails. Meridian's boundary tests verify behavior. An engineering success-rate improvement remains unmeasured.

Yao et al. · 2023 · v3

ReAct

Actions need observations. The coordinator adapts from actual tool results. Meridian exposes action and result events and summaries. It does not reproduce private thought traces.

Barres et al. · 2025 · v1

τ²-bench

The user acts in the same environment. Shared-state tasks motivated concurrent-user edits, revision conflict checks and final-state assertions. Deterministic interleaving tests do not reproduce the paper's user simulator.

Xia et al. · 2024 · v1

Agentless

More autonomy needs evidence. A simple parser and fixed verification and recovery rules provide an honest baseline. Development subagent count does not measure runtime design quality.

Liu et al. · 2023 · v3

Lost in the Middle

More context is not automatically better. Bounded observations and explicit memory queries keep relevant state inspectable. The current character limits are engineering choices, not optima proved by the paper.

Proposed

A future live benchmark

Start from explicit requirements and independently reviewed targets. Give Meridian and a general agent the same toolchain, repeat trials, and measure final-state acceptance separately from time, provider cost, invalid actions and unknown evidence. Hardware performance needs physical measurements of its own.

Architecture

Check tiers and trust states

Each tier has a time budget and a trigger. A design moves to the next tier only when the one before it passes. Rev B adds data consistency to T0, process-derived fits and a tolerance stack to T1, thermal life and the torque-speed-voltage check to T2, and bench templates to T4.

The cheapest new check catches the failure seen on real boards. Data consistency runs in milliseconds at T0, before any solver.

TierBudgetRunsChecks for the actuator
T0 StaticmillisecondsEvery editSource compiles. Units agree. Every requirement has a check and a bench step. Electrical rules pass. Both sides of each port and contract match. Part number, symbol, footprint, 3D body and BOM line agree for every component. Every module's license class is allowed for this product. Fits come from the capability pack, so an H7 seat in a printed part fails here.
T1 Geometry and rulessecondsEvery commitParts regenerate. No interference through a full input revolution. Board clears its pocket by 0.5 mm. Encoder chip within 0.25 mm of the shaft axis. Compiled .kicad_dru rules for the phase current and bus voltage. A kernel-tied Monte Carlo tolerance stack for backlash and the pilot fit. Parts in stock.
T2 PhysicsminutesBefore reviewCircuit simulation at tolerance corners. Motor torque against speed and bus voltage, from the motor curve and the current limit. Driver junction temperature at stall. Contact stress on lobes and pins at tolerance corners. A disc-temperature bound for polymer reducers. Firmware current loop against a 2-phase stepper plant.
T3 Search and long runshoursOn request, overnightFull placement and routing by solvers. Multibody simulation of the reducer for efficiency and torque ripple. Sweeps across ratio, bus voltage and layer count. Mutation runs of the check suite.
T4 BenchdaysEach physical buildDoggo's continuous-torque test. Roozing's 90-minute run-in and 10-hour endurance block, with play and friction measured before and after. Per-motor system identification in the ToddlerBot style. A disc-temperature log. Reports are hashed to firmware and script and flagged when two runs are not comparable. Differences recalibrate T2 and T3 and write back to the registry.

Datum's evidence engine: nothing is ever called verified

One reviewer put it this way: a green badge over a nominal model is worse than no badge, because it removes the engineer's paranoia, and the paranoia is the real safety system. So a requirement moves along a ladder, and only hardware reaches the top.

Inputs, with their source

Every result lists the numbers it used and where each came from, so a reviewer can see what was assumed.

Bands, not points

An uncertain input is evaluated across its range. If the limit is crossed anywhere, the check fails and names the input.

What was not checked

Listed beside every pass. A check with no geometry reports skipped, never pass.

What Meridian's engines can actually establish

DomainImplemented evidenceWhat remains outside the result
MechanicalCadQuery and OpenCascade B-rep solids. Box, cylinder, profile extrusion, hole, Boolean and fillet features. Fixed, revolute and prismatic mates. Static interference and bounded discrete motion checks. STEP and STL.Continuous swept-collision proof, FEA, fatigue, tolerance stack-up, full-arm inverse kinematics and synthetic-muscle physics.
PCBEditable two-layer rectangular boards. A pin and net graph. Routes, vias and bounded routing. Local geometry and connectivity. Native KiCad DRC. These distinctions matter. A collision pass concerns the modeled bodies and checked poses. A DRC pass concerns the declared layout and rules. A compiled HDL file may still be functionally wrong. Generic gates are not a foundry-ready chip.

Parts that are only a mesh, from the Datum design notes

Numbers travel as text. Images are for pointing.

You asked how to tokenize a 3D model so an agent knows what each part is. The honest finding is that you do not. Every mesh tokenizer in the literature needs a model fine-tuned to read it, and a frozen GPT or Claude reads only text and images. Models also estimate dimensions badly from pictures: one benchmark scored 0.84 on questions about CAD code and 0.59 on the same questions from renders.

So Datum turns geometry into measured facts, at three levels of detail, and puts the same short ids on the pictures so text and image refer to the same thing.

LevelWhat the agent getsWhen
L0One line per part: name, size, mass, roleAlways in context
L1The part card: features, candidate interfaces, matches to standardsFetched per part
L2Individual surfaces, measurements, sections, marked rendersAsked for with a query tool
  1. Read what the file already says. Product names, the assembly tree, colours.
  2. Measure the whole. Size, volume, centre of mass, symmetry, whether the mesh is closed, and a guess at the unit with a confidence.
  3. Find the surfaces. Split the mesh at sharp edges and fit planes, cylinders, cones and spheres, each with its fit error.
  4. Apply rules. A concave cylinder open at both ends is a through hole. Four equal holes on a square are a pattern. A transition two facets wide is "fillet or chamfer", never a guess.
  5. Snap to standards, and report the miss. 3.4 mm is an M3 clearance hole. Four of them on a 31 mm square around a 22 mm pilot is a NEMA 17 face.
  6. Propose interfaces. Each becomes a candidate port with its frame and the evidence for it.
  7. Name things last. A vision model sees marked views and picks from a closed vocabulary. The name is kept only if it agrees with the geometry.

Identity without a feature tree

A named face is the surface it lies on: a plane's normal and offset, a cylinder's axis and radius. After any rebuild the name resolves to whatever lies on that surface, and zero matches is reported as a broken reference. One study measured this at 100% reference retention against 32–47% for index-based selection. The same rule gives mesh-only parts stable ids.

How parts connect

Candidates come from geometry: opposed flat faces in contact, coaxial cylinders, matching hole patterns. The agent chooses among enumerated candidates. It never outputs a pose. Choosing among candidates scored 72% in one study; regressing poses scored 46%.

Architecture

Open toolchain specifics

Rev A named the tools. This table pins the versions, licenses and limits that decide whether each one can carry a product.

Most layers have an open choice that can carry a product, each with a license or maturity limit to design around. Tolerance stacks and the motor plant have nothing usable, so you build them.
