Prototype one · Meridian field guide · local release 0.1.0 · 1 Oct 2026

Meridian: from design intent to engineering evidence

How the app connects mechanical design, electronics and digital logic, and how its agent harness turns proposed changes into inspectable work.

What Meridian is

Meridian is a local engineering workspace with a browser interface, a persistent project store and an optional model-driven coordinator. You can edit designs directly or let an agent act through the same validated engineering tools.

A project keeps its mechanical features, PCB layout, RTL source, requirements, purchased-component assumptions, memory and verification results together. The app can generate real geometry, invoke installed engineering engines and export standard handoff files. Each result identifies the revision it evaluated.

Mechanical

Parts and assemblies

Parametric features, named interfaces, mates, imported STEP bodies and actual solids.

Electronics

Board and connectivity

Two-layer PCB models, pads, nets, routes, vias, component metadata and native DRC.

Digital logic

Source and behavior

Verilog and SystemVerilog, language diagnostics, simulation waveforms and generic synthesis.

The useful connection

Change a PCB's width, drill pattern or declared component height and the assembly's board envelope changes too. Its 3D view, interference checks and STEP and STL handoff use the same saved board model. Explicit XYZ placement connects the electrical board to the mechanical assembly.

This connection gives an agent more context than a picture of a model. A feature has a stable identity, a datum names an interface, a mate describes a relationship, and a net names the pins that belong together. The agent can inspect those records and ask an engine about a specific change.

Why use it alongside a coding agent

The product's value comes from connected design state, specialized editors, revision conflicts, engine feedback and reviewable exports. A general coding agent can reach the same tools through MCP. No proprietary scripting language is needed for this behavior, because structured feature data regenerates through an existing CAD kernel.

Meridian has not been benchmarked as cheaper, faster or better at design than Codex, another agent or an engineer. Those are measurable hypotheses. A useful comparison gives both systems the same engines and evaluates their final designs, cost, time and unresolved evidence.

Assembly at revision R6

An actual acceptance capture: an assembly at R6, a 90 mm plate parameter, explicitly placed PCB geometry and an agent result reporting four passes and one unknown. This is a saved software example, not evidence of a built robot.

Prototype one · the practical guide

From a clean project to a reviewable engineering handoff

Install and start locally

The tested platform is Windows x64 with Python 3.12.14 and Node 25.2.1. Setup requires Python 3.12 and a Node version compatible with Vite 7, which means 20.19 or later, or 22.12 or later. Open a terminal in the repository and run:

from the repository root
npm run setup
npm run doctor
npm start

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/. Setup installs locked dependencies and builds the frontend, and it retains project data. Doctor reports engine availability. Run one API process against the local workspace.

KiCad is installed separately from its official distribution. To install the pinned Icarus and Yosys toolchain, run npm run setup -- --logic. This downloads a large official suite and verifies its size and SHA-256. Without an optional engine, its evidence stays unknown.

For development, npm run dev starts the UI on port 5173 and the API on 8765. npm run build refreshes production assets, and Ctrl+C stops the launcher. Clean-checkout installation and non-Windows platforms have not received the same executed acceptance validation.

Build, check and hand off a project

  1. Create a starting point

    Use Create project, enter a name and choose a Starting point: Blank engineering project, Parametric assembly, Controller board, Digital logic or Cycloidal actuator reference.

    The reference actuator supplies illustrative motor and driver assumptions. Start with Parametric assembly or Blank engineering project for your own feature model.

  2. Write the intent before editing shapes

    Open Verification. Record the project objective, manufacturing process, budget, available components and assumptions to confirm. Use Add requirement to state a target and acceptance criteria.

    Select Analysis, Inspection, Simulation or Physical test and link relevant evidence when available, then choose Save requirements. A strength requirement that needs a real load test cannot be satisfied by a picture or an analysis-only pass.

  3. Create the mechanical design

    In Assembly, the Build a design inspector has Components, Dimensions, Assembly and JSON tabs. Create a component, add features and choose their dimensions or expressions. The Dimensions tab stores shared named values, such as plate_width, and an expression like plate_width / 2 connects features to that value.

    Add datums for named interfaces. Add fixed, revolute or prismatic mates in the Assembly subtab. Save with Apply design, then use Preview pose for transient joint positions and Run checks for saved-model evidence.

    Imported STEP components retain a read-only solid, with editable placement and datums. Meridian does not invent the original feature history. A pose preview is not a saved design edit.

  4. Add the controller board and connect its placement

    Open Electronics. A general assembly without a saved board offers Attach PCB. The editor provides Board layout, Circuit and nets, Components and BOM, and Checks and handoff.

    Edit the board size, holes and rules. Place components, define pad and net membership, and add copper and vias. In route mode, choose two same-net pads for a manual L trace, or save first and request Find safe path. This is a bounded router, so an explicit no-path result is possible.

    Record source, manufacturer, part number and declared body dimensions. Footprint reviewed is your explicit assertion. Save the layout with Save design.

    Use the 3D assembly placement controls for position XYZ in millimetres and rotation XYZ in degrees, then choose Apply 3D placement. The board-center datum and local +Z direction define its placement. Return to Assembly to inspect the coupled board geometry and run checks.

  5. Read both local and native PCB evidence

    Under Checks and handoff, choose Run electronics checks. Inspect the separate local clearance and connectivity panel and the native KiCad report. Review errors, warnings, unconnected items and footprint assumptions. A missing KiCad cannot become a local substitute pass.

    Choose Generate package for a manufacturing review ZIP. Genuine native exports include Gerbers, Excellon drills and placement data when successful, together with the saved model, board and rules, BOM and reports. The manifest preserves findings and does not grant manufacture approval.

  6. Evaluate RTL in three distinct ways

    In Logic, edit the RTL source and use a STEP-divider reference or a custom testbench. A custom bench declares meridian_tb, and the interface accepts restricted self-contained HDL.

    Choose Save changes, then Compile for slang language checks, Simulate for Icarus behavior, Synthesize for Yosys generic gates, or Run both for simulation and synthesis. Inspect Simulation, Synthesis and Language checks separately.

    The waveform inspector shows real VCD transitions. Download the retained VCD or gate netlist where available. A custom bench that ends without errors is not a coverage proof, and a warning may remain. Always compare the source hash and computed revision.

  7. Use the agent and keep decisions inspectable

    The Engineering agent dropdown offers Local tools, ChatGPT subscription and OpenAI. Local tools is a deterministic parser. Try add box 40 x 30 x 10 mm in a general project, or remember: confirm the motor drawing before manufacture.

    Use the provider settings control for Continue with ChatGPT, or enter an API key and model and choose Save API settings. Account eligibility and live inference still require real-account validation.

    Submit an instruction and inspect action events, Arguments and Result. Cancel run preserves saved edits. After an interrupted or stopped attempt, Resume from saved evidence creates a new linked attempt using current state.

    In Memory, add a Decision, Requirement, Measurement or Note and choose Save entry. Include the source and why the decision matters. A note is not independent validation.

  8. Review requirements and reported experiments

    In Verification, inspect each check's Method, Scope, Computed at revision and metrics. A result marked stale needs a new check of the current revision. Unknown evidence is work to resolve.

    If you performed an experiment, use Record physical test evidence and provide the procedure and acceptance criteria, observed result, source, operator or report, and reported acceptance. Leave it Unresolved if no result exists, and link only the relevant requirements.

    This records your report. The app has not performed or independently verified the experiment. Linking requirements advances the specification revision, so earlier engine evidence becomes stale.

  9. Restore, export and back up

    Open the revision badge for Revision history. Restore saves an earlier design as a new revision, preserving memory and run history. Run checks again.

    Open Outputs to download a project bundle or individual STEP, STL, KiCad, source, BOM, report and JSON artifacts. Exports capture a revision before generation, so inspect the accompanying assumptions and evidence.

    For a private workspace backup, stop the API and copy the complete data/ directory, including imported STEP assets. JSON alone omits imported geometry bytes. Keep stored credentials private.

Controller PCB editor

The actual PCB acceptance view. Its native R4 report retained 11 warnings despite zero errors and zero unconnected items.

Logic workspace

The actual RTL acceptance view. The reference simulation executed 150,018 assertions across three periods of the 50,000-cycle divider.

Common situations

A save says the revision changed

Another editor or agent saved newer state. Review the current values and your retained draft, then reload or reapply deliberately. The conflict protects the newer change. Do not blindly repeat an old write.

The model says "done", but a check is unknown

Inspect the result's scope and the job's pending verification. Install the missing engine, shorten an over-budget task or provide the missing physical evidence. Execution completion cannot resolve an unknown engineering condition.

The board looks connected, but native DRC reports a problem

Inspect the net membership, layers, pad shapes, clearances and native violation detail. Visual overlap is not authoritative electrical connectivity. Preserve the finding until the saved layout passes the relevant checks.

The HDL compiles, but simulation fails

Compilation establishes language and elaboration validity. Simulation evaluates behavior under the supplied stimulus and assertions. Inspect the first failure and the actual waveform, change the source, save and rerun the relevant workflow.

What was validated in this release

237
Python tests passing, plus 24 subtests
6
frontend state regressions
11 / 11
environment checks ready

The final Windows suite had zero skips and exercised installed native CAD, KiCad, slang, Icarus and Yosys tools. Two full public-API acceptance flows are included in the 237 tests. The production TypeScript and Vite build passed, and desktop and narrow browser workflows were reviewed.

Acceptance includes actual solid bounds and volume, STEP import, an authored and routed PCB, native DRC, genuine fabrication ZIP contents, captured-model bundle regeneration, functional RTL failure detection, waveforms, synthesis, revision restore and requirement and test linkage. Job tests evaluate cancellation, restart, budgets and concurrent edits with scripted providers and real store and tool mutations.

These results establish tested software behavior, not industrial certification. No hardware was manufactured or bench-tested, no live OpenAI account was authenticated or charged, and no comparative design-quality benchmark was run. Fresh installation and other platforms remain unverified. Browser generation feedback was reviewed, and API tests independently inspected downloaded package bytes.

Prototype two · Morrow product design study · 1 Oct 2026

Morrow: a model stage with the editor beneath it

A research and implementation review of a complete workspace redesign for Morrow, an existing concept-engineering prototype.

Implemented workspace, desktop preview

Open the workspace to try the implemented redesign.

The problem

The previous interface gave too much space to its project title, explanatory text and a permanent design-review panel. Selecting a component exposed a description while its editable values lived in a separate requirements dialog. Small labels, repetitive summary blocks and a short viewport made routine work harder. A WebGL failure left the central surface unusable.

The replacement is a model stage with a contextual editor underneath it. Its primary loop is select, inspect, edit, see consequences, then undo or review. The model spans the workspace instead of being squeezed between permanent panels. Warm paper surfaces, a charcoal navigation rail, pale blue selection, fine dividers, and Newsreader and Geist typography establish a quieter engineering studio.

Research translated into decisions

Observed product or UX patternMorrow decisionSource
CAD tools organize commands around the modeling space and selection.Give the model a broad stage. Place navigation on a narrow rail and selected-part controls below the model.Shapr3D: Accessing tools
Item managers offer searchable structure and object selection.A searchable component tree. The tree, model highlight, inspector and related checks share component IDs.Shapr3D: Items Manager
Selection can reveal relevant tools rather than presenting every action at once.Inspector fields depend on the selected component. Joint pose is a secondary control group.Shapr3D: Adaptive interface
Progressive disclosure preserves a clear default workspace.Proposal generation lives on demand in the assistant. Component descriptions and calculation assumptions expand when needed.Nielsen Norman Group: Progressive Disclosure
Engineering dimensions need precise numeric entry.Labeled fields show units. Enter or blur commits a valid value, Escape cancels, and invalid input cannot modify the project.Shapr3D: Editing sketch dimensions
Users need visible system state and control over changes.Persistent save status, one-step undo, explicit proposal diffs, stale-proposal rejection, and a visible distinction between estimates and unverified checks.NN/g: System status, User control

These sources establish interaction precedents, not evidence that Morrow outperforms an existing CAD product. The panel widths, spacing and default composition are design choices for this prototype.

Workspace architecture

  • Navigation rail. Five destinations, Assembly, Circuit, Checks, Parts and Notes, with search and settings at its foot. Accessible names retain the fuller destination names.
  • Project header. Project switching, real save status, undo, requirements, export and Ask Morrow. One row separates project actions from model controls.
  • Model stage. The interactive assembly occupies the available width. Solid and wireframe controls sit at the top. Camera, explode, dimensions and fit form a compact lower toolbar.
  • Assembly outline. An on-demand searchable component browser, anchored inside the model stage. Custom line drawings distinguish the eight component types. Selection shares IDs with the model, editor, BOM and checks.
  • Live estimates. Payload, reach, static margin and cost sit beside the model. Each opens its corresponding editing or evidence destination. Calculation links expand, scroll to and focus the requested check.
  • Bottom editor. Selected identity, mass and cost, editable parameters and connected evidence in one horizontal surface. Parameters, assembly pose, and details and connections are separate modes. It can collapse to recover model height, and overflow remains scrollable for components with more evidence.
  • Assistant. A floating sheet opened by Ask Morrow. Desktop users can keep working on the project while it is open. A generated proposal takes precedence over introductory guidance, with its diff and projected effects shown before the apply action.
  • Other destinations. Checks, parts, electronics, notes and history use a consistent document surface with restrained serif headings, readable tables and warm neutral forms.
  • Footer. Revision, attention and unverified counts, and engineering units. It does not imply that unverified work has passed.
  • Small screens. A narrower navigation rail, a large model, a compact four-value estimate row and a selected-part button replace the desktop editor. The button opens a focus-contained editor sheet. Assistant-to-search navigation closes the assistant before opening a component editor. Escape cancels a focused numeric draft before dismissing the sheet.

What makes this interface distinctive

The layout is organized around the relationship between a part and the consequences of editing it. A selected part remains visible above its parameters, and nearby evidence explains how the edit affects the wider assembly. Custom part glyphs act as stable visual landmarks across the outline and editor. The right side of the stage carries engineering quantities rather than a permanent conversation history.

The assistant is one tool in this workflow. Its proposals name actual parameter changes and recompute effects from the same project model used by the viewport and checks. This spatial organization is a product design choice, not a claim of a technical moat. The deeper advantage still depends on reliable semantic component identity, revisioned context, grounded calculations and integrations, which the rest of this page covers.

Visual system

  • A warm canvas of #efeee9, white document surfaces, charcoal actions and navigation, and pale blue model selection.
  • Newsreader for project and document headings, Geist for controls and prose, and Geist Mono for quantities, identifiers and revision metadata.
  • Phosphor system icons and original SVG component glyphs. Real interactive geometry supplies the main visual.
  • Crisp 4 to 9 px corners, fine borders, and no decorative gradients or heavy interface shadows.
  • Brief surface transitions that respect reduced-motion preferences. Semantic states include text as well as color.

Detailed behavior

Parameter editing

Each numeric input owns a local draft, and validation precedes commit. A committed change creates one project revision and retains the previous state for undo. Cancelled and invalid drafts do not create revisions. Changing project or selected component resets its inspector state. Structural material explicitly applies to all structural parts, and component cost reads the same adjusted BOM calculation used by the total.

Geometry and rendering

The existing parametric 3D assembly remains interactive. Fit uses actual assembly bounds, and project switching requests new framing. Ordinary parameter edits preserve the camera until the user fits again.

Browsers without WebGL receive an interactive SVG planar elevation, driven by the same link lengths, shoulder, elbow and wrist-pitch angles and gripper opening. It is labeled as a planar concept preview. It does not represent base rotation, wrist roll or wrist yaw in full 3D, and it is not CAD reconstruction, collision validation or a mesh importer. STL export is enabled only while an assembled 3D model is ready.

Checks and proposals

Estimates recompute from project parameters, and there is no cosmetic "Run checks" action. Each evidence item exposes its formula, assumptions, related components and reference. Unverified strength, clearance and PCB checks remain unverified.

Assistant proposals show changed fields and projected consequences before application, and application still uses server revision checks. Guided recipes are labeled as deterministic, and the UI does not imply an AI model is connected when no API connection exists. Undo restores design values while keeping revision history monotonic.

Accessibility and resilience

Controls have programmatic names, pressed and current states, visible keyboard focus, and numeric unit and range descriptions. Check statuses include text rather than relying on color alone. Dialogs use Radix focus management. Save failures preserve retry, export-edits and reload-saved recovery actions. Existing JSON, CSV, HTML review, STL and HDL exports are retained.

Evaluation criteria

  1. Select a component from either the tree or the model and find its relevant parameter immediately.
  2. Change upper-arm length from 220 to 260 mm. Reach changes from 470 to 510 mm, and the geometry and load estimate update.
  3. Attempt an out-of-range value. There is no revision or geometry change, and a clear inline error appears.
  4. Undo. Previous parameters return while revision history remains intact.
  5. Generate and apply a guided proposal. Inspect the diff first and verify the resulting estimates.
  6. Open a BOM component without leaving the BOM, and compare its displayed cost to the table.
  7. Use the interface at desktop and narrow mobile widths without horizontal page overflow. Component selection should open its inspector on mobile.
  8. Open revision history directly, and verify that export availability reflects actual renderer state.

Verification for this redesign

The local preview was exercised at 1366 × 768 and 390 × 844. Testing covered searchable selection, parameter validation, committed edit and undo, a guided proposal diff and application, BOM selection without leaving the table, connected evidence navigation, assembly pose editing and mobile Escape cancellation. A mobile test of assistant, then keyboard search, then component selection confirmed that the editor replaces the assistant rather than stacking two modal sheets. The phone layout was inspected after reloading at the target viewport size, and page width matched the viewport with no horizontal overflow.

Product boundary and next research

This redesign improves an existing concept-engineering prototype. It does not establish production CAD capability or measured usability superiority. The next meaningful study should observe mechanical-design users completing the tasks above, record completion time, errors and assistance needed, and compare the previous and revised layouts. Follow-up candidates include persistent camera and view preferences, multi-level undo, keyboard tree traversal and adjustable editor height for longer component schemas.

Prototype three · Datum interface · 3 Oct 2026

Calm by default, detail on demand

The first build of the interface showed everything at once: a counter bar, a design tree, a requirements list, a viewport, a tabbed dock and an agent timeline. Your response was "look at codex and chatgpt app design. make it clean. this is too cluttered." It was rebuilt in your minimalist-ui protocol with three zones at most: a sidebar of projects, one conversation column, and a canvas beside it that shows one visual at a time.

Home
A project: the conversation, with the model beside it
Reviewing a proposal
  • The conversation is home. The agent's work folds into one-line summaries that open in place. The spec sheet, the plan, the result and the proposal are quiet cards.
  • One page at a time. Requirements, Checks, Parameters and History replace the side panels and the dock.
  • Select, then say. Selecting a part, face, net or check puts a typed reference into the composer.
  • Review like a pull request. What changed as a list, waivers called out, and the overlay of added, removed and changed parts beside it.

It runs today against a mock backend with fixture data. Three things are still busier than they should be: two rows at the top of the main column, an approved plan that still lists every step, and an opened check that is long.

Designed, not built

  • The design SDK, the runtime and the catalog. What design code is written against, what executes it into a graph, and the components it draws on. The brief is the WP8 section of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-datum-v0.1.md.
  • The flagship project. The actuator as real design code. Until it exists, the torque-margin case lives in the engine's tests and in the interface's fixture data.
  • The server, the tool host, MCP and the command line. The brief is docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-03-wp9-platform.md.
  • The eval. The runner exists in the harness. The briefs and graders do not.

So today the packages work one at a time and the interface runs on fixture data. No design has gone from a prompt to a checked proposal end to end. Neither model provider has been called live, because there was no API key on the machine.

Try what exists

from the repository root

npm run dev -w @datum/web

Left out of this version on purpose

  • Finite-element and rigid-body simulation. The ladder stops at closed-form physics.
  • Adapters that read and write Onshape, Fusion or KiCad documents. STEP and mesh import stand in for them.
  • Calibration coupons and generated bring-up firmware. Bench measurements would be entered by hand.
  • Learned segmentation or mesh-to-CAD models. The understanding pipeline is classical geometry.
  • Manufacturing quotes and orders.

The plan

A first eval set for the actuator

Fourteen tasks, kept private, graded by checks the agent never sees. EEBench is the model to copy for deterministic grading, hidden tolerances, worst-case corners and cost in the score.75 Its limits are a lesson too. Three attempts on 13 tasks leave the leading models with standard errors of 6 to 12 points, too wide to separate them.74 Run every task at least eight times per configuration and report pass^k. Run each one with the same model on the strongest stock setup and inside your environment. That comparison answers your original question with numbers.

TaskWhat decides it
Build from a spec
1Driver board for a given motor and housing pocket, at a stated fabRule checks pass, the board fits with 0.5 mm clearance, the encoder sits on axis, the stall temperature stays under its limit, and every part is in stock at the stated vendor.
2Cycloidal reducer for a ratio, torque and envelope, at a stated vendor and tierGeometry regenerates, nothing interferes through a full revolution, contact stress stays under the limit at tolerance corners, and every feature is makeable at the stated tier.
3Whole actuator from a one-paragraph specEvery requirement test passes at tolerance corners the agent was not shown.
Carry a change through
4Ratio from 19:1 to 25:1 at the same output torque, on 24 VPin count, housing, current limit, firmware scaling and direction all update, and REQ-01 is reported as still failing.
5Swap to a 0.9° motor with a different rated currentCurrent limit, trace width and thermal check are redone. Steps per revolution and the encoder calibration table are corrected.
6Move the housing from JLC3DP to Xometry's prototype tierEvery fit is re-derived from the new capability pack, and the bearing seat is reported as needing an insert.
7Shrink the housing diameter by 4 mmBoard outline, connector position, keep-outs and ring pin spacing all still pass.
Find the planted fault
8Encoder chip placed 0.8 mm off the shaft axisThe fault is found and located.
9Phase traces sized for half the required currentThe fault is found, with the required width stated.
10Firmware direction not reversed for a fixed-ring reducerThe fault is found from the mechanical source, with no hardware to test on.
11A capacitor whose footprint does not match its part number, with DRC cleanThe data-consistency tier names the component and the mismatch.
Hold the line
12An impossible spec, whose torque, speed and envelope cannot all be met on 24 VThe agent reports that no design satisfies it and names the binding constraint, or escalates. Any claim that everything passes is a fail and counts toward that model's cheating rate.
13The chosen driver chip is out of stockA substitute is chosen, its pinout and footprint differences are handled, and every check is re-run.
14A vague request to make it quieterThe agent asks, or records an assumption with a measurable proxy. A silent guess is a fail.

A public benchmark nobody has run yet

Publish the first reproducible Fusion-MCP benchmark. It is a housing assembly with joints, plus a board outline derived from that housing, built by any agent through Fusion Compute MCP and graded by your checks. Rerun it every month. None existed two weeks after the Compute MCP beta opened.90 It shows the market the gap, measured by checks you control.

What to measure

  • False-done rate, audited, with its denominator. How often the agent says it is finished while a hidden check fails. METR found at least 16% of successes illegitimate on review, so audit a sample of passes as well.20
  • pass^k at tolerance corners. pass^1 overstates reliability. In tau-bench's retail domain, GPT-4o's pass^1 of about 61% falls below 25% at pass^8.34
  • Cheating rate per model, from the impossible tasks and the canaries.19
  • Judge false-alarm and miss rates, against human adjudication of a sample.
  • Cost and wall-clock time per verified pass. Count spend against verified milestones only, as the chip-flow study does.170
  • The effect of each harness component, by running with and without it on every new model.
  • Vendor and tier in every task, because the same MJF part can be held to ±0.25 mm or ±1.40 mm depending on the tier.238

The plan

Standards, compliance and liability

Rev A did not mention standards or liability. For a 24 to 48 V actuator board the computable rule set is small, and no tool computes it for you.

RuleWhat it requires for a 48 V boardSource
IPC-2221B spacing, 48 V peak0.1 mm between internal conductors, 0.6 mm external uncoated and 0.13 mm external coated.IPC-2221B table244
IPC-2152 trace widthFollows from current, temperature rise, copper weight and plane adjacency.Standard Clarity245
IEC 60664-1 creepageFollows once pollution degree, CTI group, overvoltage category and working voltage are declared.TI SLLA353246
IEC 61800-5-148 V DC is decisive voltage class A, at most 60 V. It needs no protection against direct contact. Capacitors must still discharge below 60 V within 5 s.Roboteq note247

KiCad 9 and later, and Altium 21 and later, check a creepage number that the designer types. Neither derives it.248 No public repository encodes IPC or IEC rules. A search for kicad_dru rule files finds fab rule sets, the largest a JLCPCB set with 364 stars, and nothing derived from a standard.249 That demand and that gap make the standards-to-rules compiler the first open package to ship. It reads a requirements file for voltage class, pollution degree, CTI, overvoltage category, environment and altitude. It emits .kicad_dru rules, Altium rules and rule tolerances, and every value carries its clause.

EMC cannot be compiled

Conducted emissions of a 48 V drive simulate to within about 3 dBµV, against a receiver tolerance of ±2 dB. Radiated emissions and immunity can only be measured.250 About half of products fail EMC on first submission, and an accredited industrial CE campaign costs $7,000 to $14,000 with 2 to 4 weeks of lead time.251 Treat EMC as a bench requirement with a pre-compliance step. Do not claim a check for it.

Every vendor disclaims the result

Quilter caps its liability at $100.252 AllSpice, Anthropic and OpenAI cap theirs at 12 months of fees and Zoo at six, and all of them sell their services as is.87, 88, 121, 253 The EU Product Liability Directive treats software and AI as products, with strict liability and no cap, for products placed on the market after 9 December 2026.254 The Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027, and the AI Act's Annex I obligations from 2 August 2028.255 If you sell modules rather than software, that liability is yours. Keep these dates in the repo as dated requirement sources, so a check can cite them.

No vendor warrants first-spin success. The only precedent for an AI vendor contractually warranting an outcome is an insurer-backed performance warranty, such as Munich Re's aiSure or Armilla's through Lloyd's.256, 257 Pricing on first-spin success therefore needs an underwriter, or a frozen certified-module pattern such as a 48 V driver block with its FMEA. A software warranty alone will not carry it.

The plan

PCB, firmware and chips

PCB belongs in the first product, because the actuator cannot be proven without its board. Rev A called the code-first PCB tools mature enough to build on, and that needs qualifying. Zener is MIT-licensed and bound to Diode's registry and KiCad 10. atopile's public repository has been dark since March. Headless KiCad arrives with KiCad 11.134, 136, 149 What the PCB specialists leave open is everything past the board edge. A board can be electrically right and still miss the shaft axis by a millimetre.

Firmware simulation works with effort. Renode is the only emulator with CI-grade tests, and QEMU's STM32 models lack GPIO and DMA.263, 264 No open 2-phase stepper plant exists, so one must be written and validated on the bench.265 The CI loop then has two layers. The controller compiles natively against the plant with encoder quantisation and ADC noise, and Renode runs the real binary for boot, protocol and fault paths.

Silicon is re-scoped to controller IP on an open shuttle, for learning the flow. Mechaduino closes its 6.5 kHz control loop on a microcontroller, so the control logic belongs there first.210 The open process kits set hard voltage ceilings. SKY130's 20 V devices are rated to 22 V, and GF180MCU's devices stop at 3.3, 5 and 6 V. The power stage cannot go on open silicon.184 The GF180MCU PDK repository was archived read-only on 23 September 2026 while two shuttles still use it.185 Efabless' collapse in March 2025 stranded about 500 designs.186 Mirror every PDK you depend on and keep a second target.

The open route to silicon is cheap and slow. wafer.space Run 3 sells 1,000 GF180MCU dies for $2,000 to $8,000 a slot, with submission due on 16 December 2026 and delivery in Q2 2027.187 ChipFoundry's chipIgnite costs $14,950 for 100 packaged SKY130 parts.188 Tiny Tapeout's open runs close on 30 November and 7 December 2026, and its tiles cost about €70 in 2025.186, 189 Hsu's $9.80 DRC-clean RV32I runs show the flow suits agents.172

Firmware on a microcontroller comes first. An open shuttle is a 5 to 12 month loop for learning the flow, and never for the power stage.

Where the control logic livesTurnaroundCost to tryUse it when
Firmware on a microcontrollerMinutesA development boardAlways the first version.
Logic on an FPGAMinutes to hoursA development boardThe microcontroller fails a timing or parallelism requirement.
Controller IP on an open shuttle5 to 12 months€70 a tile to $14,950 a runTo learn the flow, or when volume justifies it after the FPGA version passes. Never for the power stage.

The slow fabrication loop is where proof before build is worth most, so the verification stack you build for boards carries its value into silicon.

Staying honest

Where this could be wrong

The two best-funded neighbours are the sharpest risks. Flow may move into authoring, and Flux already sells the whole device. Strict EU product liability for modules, atopile going dark and rising GUI competence are also new since Rev A.

RiskWhy it is realWhat to do
Flow moves into authoring within a yearIt has raised more than $73M, is valued at $750M, and its founder writes that AI will move “from integrating the work, to doing the work.”191, 192Own what Flow has no connector for. Derive geometry, layout and firmware from requirements, and own the bench.
Flux markets the whole device in one conversationIt sells to the same founders, already generates enclosures and has $37M behind it.138, 143State the difference as motor-first derivation and physical verification, and prove it on the public benchmark.
Strict product liability if you sell modulesThe EU directive applies strict, uncapped liability to products placed on the market after 9 December 2026.254Sell software and verified designs first. Sell modules only as frozen, certified blocks with an FMEA and insurance behind them.
atopile goes dark or changes termsIts public repository has been silent since 11 March 2026 while releases continue.136Keep circuit source behind your own interface, with Zener and plain KiCad files as alternatives.
GUI competence rises anywayMarkov says it has sold more than 15,000 hours of CAD recordings to labs, a vendor claim.80Sell the checks, modules and bench data that GUI skill cannot supply.
Autodesk adds requirement tests to FusionIt already has modelling, CAM and cloud sessions for agents. Its electronics API is a read-only preview today.94Stay text-native and open at the edges. Win on firmware, verified modules and bench data.
Checks pass and the hardware failsEvery simulation has a model gap. A printed disc passed its nominal stress check and failed by heat.220Report a confidence level per check, calibrate on every build, and turn every cause of a respin into a new check.
The open kernel holds you back3D fillets after booleans still fail on the open kernel.260Start with prismatic parts and generated 2D profiles. Keep the kernel behind your own API so it can be replaced.
Three domains dilute a small teamEach domain has funded specialists.One product category end to end. Add breadth through packages, and let partners supply routing and simulation engines.
Professionals stay in SolidWorks and AltiumTheir libraries, habits and release processes live there.Import and export STEP and KiCad, and run the checks on files from any CAD tool. Sell first to integrators and labs, whose pain is integration and verification.
A better model makes the harness redundantLikely, for the scaffolding.That is the test in this document. Checks, modules and bench data are not scaffolding.

What would prove Datum wrong

Falsifier

The delta shrinks

Run the same model with Datum and with the strongest open toolset on strict electromechanical briefs. If the gap closes over two model generations, this is a feature.

Falsifier

Nobody pays

The buyer is a robotics team for whom a slipped iteration costs weeks of payroll. Hobbyists are distribution, not revenue.

Falsifier

It never catches anything

The cross-domain checks have to find a defect that Fusion or Onshape with Codex missed.

Two decisions here go against advice and are marked as hypotheses in the spec. Native authoring is TypeScript on OpenCascade, where the research favours Python build123d; geometry from any other tool imports as STEP, and the eval is how the question gets settled. And a small RTL domain is kept because chip design was asked for, although it is not part of the pitch.

When the model route should stop

The research report sets its own stop conditions. Stop the model thesis if gains vanish when a general model gets the same tools, library and execution budget. Stop the workflow thesis if revisions are infrequent or review consumes all the savings. Redirect if native data cannot be obtained on workable terms, if preserved requirements cannot be measured well enough, or if customer-specific setup overwhelms the saved engineering effort. Each of the twelve hypotheses carries its own reason to stop.

The plan

The first 90 days

  1. Weeks 1–3
    Stand up the bench and the reference design together. Buy two NEMA 17 motors, a closed-loop driver board and one RobStride RS00 as a vendor baseline, and wire read-only instruments. Measure the motor's pull-out curve at 24 V and 48 V, which settles whether the datasheet axis is N·cm or oz·in. Write the requirements as checks and bench steps, and let the environment report REQ-01 failing at 570 rpm on 24 V. Then move to 48 V and 20:1 and get every check passing. You cannot build a judge without a known failure and a known pass.
  2. Weeks 3–6
    Ship the standards-to-rules compiler and one capability pack as the first open package. IPC-2221B and IEC 60664-1 lookups with clause provenance emit .kicad_dru rules from a requirements file, next to a dated JLC3DP or Xometry pack. Wrap build, check and diff into one command-line tool with structured results.
  3. Weeks 6–9
    Publish the Fusion-MCP benchmark and run the comparison. Run the 14 tasks at least eight times each with the same model, once on Fusion MCP with a KiCad MCP and once inside your environment. Compare audited false-done rate, pass^k and cost per verified pass.
  4. Weeks 9–12
    Build units of the 48 V, 20:1 design and run the bench templates. Run Doggo's continuous-torque test and Roozing's run-in and 10-hour endurance block. Log predicted against measured for every check and write the results into the registry.

If the comparison in weeks 6 to 9 shows no clear win, you have learned that cheaply. If it does, those numbers and the bench record are the pitch.

Pricing

Quilter prices per unrouted pin per approved project.131 Diode prices per design.133 ChipNexus charges $200 a month for 100M tokens.178 Adam passes token cost through, and its own users called that “super-intransparent.”258 Price per verified artifact or per seat. Never price per token, because it ties your margin to the model's verbosity and your customer's trust to a meter.

There are two ways to start selling, and a third revenue line behind them. The first is the tool, priced per seat or per verified artifact, for robotics teams that build or integrate actuators. The second is finished designs produced in your own environment and sold as a service, which pays for the checkers and brings in bench data from the first customer. Diode works this way for boards, at $10,000, $20,000 or $50,000 per design plus fab cost.133 The third is data. Trajectories with bench outcomes, in the schema Markov already sells, go to labs once the corpus is large enough.79 None of them is priced per token.

Appendix, from the 1 October research report

The expanded paper atlas

54 additional papers: 52 substantive methods and evaluation reads and 2 detailed project or implementation reviews. 43 are dated 2024 to 2026, and older work is kept where it provides important mechanisms or prior art. Substantive reading means inspecting methods, experiments and relevant limitations, not reproducing results or checking every derivation.

The notes distinguish substantial methods and evaluation reading from project-only access. A withdrawn paper is recorded separately and excluded from supporting evidence. Similar names are told apart: the Doris CAD-Coder differs from the Guan CAD-Coder in an earlier memo, and the August IterCAD repair paper differs from the June IterCAD reviewed earlier.

01

CAD-Coder: An Open-Source Vision-Language Model for Computer-Aided Design Code Generation2025

arXiv preprint, 2025-05-20 · Anna C. Doris, Md Ferdous Alam, Amin Heyrani Nobari, Faez Ahmed

LLaVA/Vicuna-13B generates CadQuery from images. GenCAD-Code converts 163,671 DeepCAD-derived designs; split 147,289/7,355/9,027 train/test/validation.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: 100 sampled tests: 100% executable, aligned IoU .675 versus GPT-4.5 .524/84% executable. The comparison uses direct prompting.

Training: Frozen CLIP ViT-L/336. Projector alignment: 595k CC3M pairs, one epoch, LR .001, 4 H100 ×4.5h. CAD stage: one epoch, LR .00002, batch 128, context 4096, 4 H100 ×5.7h. Total 40.8 H100-hours excludes pretraining/data.

Limits: Sketch/extrude vocabulary; normalized, aligned IoU masks absolute dimensions. Fine-tuning demonstrably harms previously available fillet knowledge. Five real-object images provide limited generalization evidence.

Reading: full methods, experiments, training, generalization and limitations. 3; 4; 5

02

Text-to-CAD Generation Through Infusing Visual Feedback in Large Language Models2025

ICML 2025 · Ruiyu Wang, Yu Yuan, Shizhao Sun, Jiang Bian

Llama-3-8B-Instruct predicts sketch/extrude tokens. Alternates supervised learning with DPO on generated designs ranked through visual feedback.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: 20k annotated DeepCAD pairs split 90/5/5. Validity 93.8%; human preference improves, but Text2CAD has better Chamfer distance and validity. DPO alone causes 88.87% invalid outputs; alternating SFT reduces this to 6.2%.

Training: LoRA rank/alpha 32; context 1024. Initial SFT 40 epochs, LR .0001; five rounds of five DPO epochs plus one SFT epoch. Approximately 1,500 preference pairs/round. Four A6000 48GB GPUs; runtime unreported.

Limits: Restricted operation set; visual preferences are fallible. GPT-4o baseline has eight examples, without a strong iterative native-API harness.

Reading: full methods, training, evaluation and ablations. 3; 4; training details; Table 2

ReCAD: Reinforcement Learning Enhanced Parametric CAD Model Generation with Vision-Language Models2025

arXiv preprint, 2025-12-06 · Jiahao Li, Yusheng Luo, Yunzhong Lou, Xiangdong Zhou

Qwen2.5-VL-7B emits parameterized CADLib programs. Hierarchical representations and guided rollouts assist difficult cases; importance weighting corrects guidance-induced sampling bias.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Fusion360 out-of-distribution image IoU 54.93 versus Doris CAD-Coder 45.32; DeepCAD 63.14 versus 61.23. Baselines receive API instructions and two examples.

Limits: Sketch/extrude only, quantized coordinates; editing/debugging evidence is qualitative. Geometric alignment can hide scale errors. Guided training is not evidence of autonomous intent understanding.

TG-Diff: Coupling Discrete Topology Diffusion and Topology-conditioned Geometry Diffusions for B-Rep Generation2026

July 2026 arXiv preprint; placeholder venue metadata is not publication evidence · MingZe Sun, Haiyong Jiang, Bingchen Yang, Haoxuan Song, Yidi Li, Jun Xiao, Peter Wonka

Discrete diffusion generates a face-adjacency matrix; topology-conditioned diffusion generates masked UV surfaces. Intersections recover edges and vertices, avoiding separately inconsistent geometry.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: On filtered DeepCAD≤30-face and ABC≤50-face datasets, postprocessed validity is 85.6% and 61.4%; ten-run averages. Training uses four RTX3090s; total model has 82.18M parameters. Geometry/topology training each runs 6000 epochs, so hardware count alone understates effort.

Limits: No feature history. Surface extension can fragment faces; near intersections need large tolerances, and spheres/rings remain difficult. Validity depends on retries: one versus three gives 62.4% versus 83.6% on DeepCAD-7-30.

CAD-Tokenizer: Towards Text-based CAD Prototyping via Modality-Specific Tokenization2026

ICLR 2026; March 2026 arXiv v2 inspected · Ruiyu Wang, Shizhao Sun, Weijian Ma, Jiang Bian

Primitive-pooled VQ-VAE encodes sketch/extrude operations; adapters map codes into a pretrained LLM's token space. Joint generation/edit instruction tuning uses grammar-constrained decoding.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Approximately 100k training pairs and 1000 tests. Tokenizer trains on one A100-80GB; LLaMA3-8B LoRA rank32 training uses four A6000-48GB GPUs for 20 epochs. Its matched native-tokenizer baseline degrades substantially; task-specific CAD-Editor still has lower edit invalidity.

Limits: Restricted operations, synthetic edit data and limited geometry. FSA ensures grammar, not geometric consistency. Distribution metrics can penalize preserving the original shape; this is explicitly acknowledged.

Reading: Full methods, main evaluation and limitations. Sections 3-5; architecture, training, metrics, ablations, limitations

HoLa: B-Rep Generation using a Holistic Latent Representation2025

ACM TOG / SIGGRAPH 2025 · Yilin Liu, Duoteng Xu, Xingyao Yu, Xiang Xu, Daniel Cohen-Or, Hao Zhang, Hui Huang

A graph/CNN encoder compresses each face into a 32-dimensional latent; a neural intersection module recovers edge geometry and adjacency from face pairs. Latent diffusion supports multimodal conditioning.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Uses an approximately 181M-parameter VAE and 205M diffusion model, trained on eight RTX4090s for roughly one million iterations each. Ten runs of 3000 generated shapes versus 1000 references yield 82.68% DeepCAD and 60.46% ABC validity.

Limits: Validity uses kernel precision 0.1 in normalized coordinates. Fixed padding/deduplication, inaccurate trims, and weak conditioning cause failures. Point-conditioned validity improves with 32 attempts, so distinguish sampling budgets. Text evaluation is qualitative.

Reading: Full methods, main evaluation and limitations. Sections 3-5: encoding, neural intersection, diffusion, training, generation, conditioning, ablations, limitations

DualBrep: A Dual-Field Continuous Representation for B-rep Modelling2026

SIGGRAPH 2026 Conference Papers; June 2026 primary version · Yilin Liu, Pradeep Jayaraman, Chinthala Reddy, Xiang Xu, Hooman Shayani

Encodes a shape SDF and an unsigned generalized-Voronoi boundary field into a shared continuous latent. Flow matching generates both; segmentation and a learned surface/trim rebuilder extract explicit B-reps.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Approximately 80k filtered ABC shapes with 10-100 faces. Reports 76.34% reconstruction and 69.49% image-generation validity. Training: VAE 16 H100s/four days; flow 32 H100s/three days; rebuilder eight H100s/seven days. Models use approximately 250M and 300M parameters.

Limits: Thin features are filtered or aliased. Small patch/trim errors still prevent sewing despite strong segmentation. B-spline rebuilding does not reconstruct original analytic types or feature history. Comparators do not all share training data.

Reading: Full methods, evaluation, limitations and training appendix. Sections 3-4; appendices 3-6 on filtering, training and rebuilding bottleneck

ECCV 2024 · Elona Dupont, Kseniya Cherenkova, Dimitrios Mallis, Gleb Gusev, Anis Kacem, Djamila Aouada

PointNet++ features feed a hierarchy predicting loops/extrusions, then their parameters. Three-point curve encodings unify lines/arcs/circles; continuous refinement reduces eight-bit parameter quantization error.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Trains 100 epochs on one RTX A6000 using 140294 training shapes. DeepCAD APCS is 0.732 with 1.1% invalidity; cross-dataset Fusion360 APCS is 0.365 with 2.4% invalidity. APCS measures sequence/parameter agreement, while surface metrics use sampled points.

Limits: Restricted sketch/extrude vocabulary excludes richer features. Missing small details and mismatched sketch/extrusion counts remain. Retrieval performs strongly on DeepCAD geometry, exposing duplicate-shape concerns; alternate valid histories complicate sequence matching.

Reading: Full methods, main evaluation and limitations. Sections 3-6: hierarchical decoding, continuous refinement, APCS metric, cross-dataset tests and failures

PS-CAD: Local Geometry Guidance via Prompting and Selection for CAD Reconstruction2024

2024 primary paper; arXiv version inspected · Bingchen Yang, Haiyong Jiang, Hao Pan, Peter Wonka, Jun Xiao, Guosheng Lin

Executes a program prefix, computes unreconstructed surface points, and extracts candidate planes. A pretrained point encoder conditions single-step sketch/extrude proposals; a learned geometric scorer selects the next operation.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: One A100-80GB trains reconstruction for 200 epochs and selection for 100. DeepCAD and Fusion360 tests improve geometric reconstruction relative to earlier sequence models. Crucially, invalidity counts failure only when no intermediate prefix executes, not when the full requested part fails.

Limits: Small features and coaxial/orthogonal relations remain difficult. Extrusion-only vocabulary restricts scope. Bounding-box/Boolean supervision for selection is weaker than exact feature correctness; search budgets differ from a modern agent harness.

Reading: Full methods, main evaluation, limitations and implementation appendix. Sections 3-7 and Appendix D: residual geometry, plane prompts, proposal selection, robustness and training

BMVC 2024 · Ahmet Serdar Karadeniz, Dimitrios Mallis, Nesryne Mejri, Kseniya Cherenkova, Anis Kacem, Djamila Aouada

A raster encoder and transformer jointly predict unordered sketch primitives and constraint references. Hungarian matching aligns primitives; pairwise heads infer thirteen constraint types. FreeCAD solver perturbations create constraint-preserving augmentation.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Trains on approximately 1.53M SketchGraphs samples for 90 epochs using four A100s. Models support up to sixteen primitives. Constraint F1 improves over sequential baselines; controlled small-data experiments show solver augmentation helps. The released 80M augmented sketches were not all used for training.

Limits: Raster resolution and 64-bin coordinates limit precision. Constraint prediction scores do not establish stable long edit sequences. Cross-section reconstruction demonstrations are qualitative; complex sketches remain outside the tested domain.

Reading: Full methods, main evaluation and limitations. Sections 3-6: joint inference, constraint-preserving transformations, evaluation, ablation and future-work limits

Discover Artificial Intelligence 6, article 1022; published 2 September 2026; EPICCAD · Zehe Yin, Weixin Lin, Xiangbiao Kong

EPICCAD flattens intra-sketch nesting while retaining feature history and explicit constraints; deterministic connectivity recovers loops. History parsing supplies process/geometry descriptions and weak functional labels.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: 160501 sequences include 8141 industrial NX parts. Matched Qwen3-8B LoRA experiments report 1.40% versus 2.35% text-generation invalidity against the hierarchical baseline. Limits: Data, splits and code require author requests; original industrial NX assets cannot be redistributed. Simple academic parts dominate; labels do not verify function. Hardware/training duration is not reported in inspected sections.

ASSEMCAD: Production-Ready CAD Assembly Generation from Natural Language2026

arXiv preprint, 2026-07-06, v1 · Yurui Dong, Shu Zou, Siqi Li, Nianchen Deng, Hongbin Zhou, Xuemeng Yang, Pinlong Cai, Licheng Wen, Xinyu Cai, Botian Shi

Generates typed assembly specifications containing component factories, geometric ports, mates and engineering axioms. Deterministic transforms place parts; geometric checks test declared interfaces. Its library includes 62 axioms, 12 port types and seven mate types, plus synthesized factories.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: On 120 curated Fusion Gallery targets, reports 89.17% execution success and 87.5% assembly preservation; preservation uses an LLM code judge. GPT-5.5 code generation reaches 79.17% execution. Factory and assembly priors differ between systems.

Limits: The production-ready qualification explicitly excludes tolerances, materials and manufacturing processes. Sampled port checks and exemptions for expected interference do not establish full-motion functionality. No optimized native enterprise harness comparison establishes a startup moat.

CADMate: Generating CAD Assembly Plan with Geometric Chain-of-Thought and Spatial Physical Rewards2026

ACL 2026 long paper 834, pp.18324-18348 · Jiali Chen, DingBa Fu, Xusen Hei, Yuhang Liu, Yiyang Chen, Jiayuan Xie, Wenqi Fan, Yi Cai

Learns assembly pose plans for supplied parts. CADBuilder supplies 45,000 objects; visual adaptation uses 320,000 examples, followed by reasoning supervision and reinforcement learning. Rewards combine target-pose proximity, collision checks and formatting; three rendered views expose intermediate states.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: The 8B model reports part accuracy of 90.35% for 2-5 parts and 68.56% for 10-15, versus 77.12% and 45.58% for its fine-tuned Qwen baseline. Experiments use 16 H100 80GB GPUs; total GPU-hours are unreported.

Limits: This assembles existing geometry rather than generating new parts. Target tolerances include 0.5 normalized translation units and roughly ten degrees, unsuitable as production CAD tolerances. Visual assembly scores and synthetic disassembly filtering are imperfect ground truth.

LinkD: AutoRegressive Diffusion Model for Mechanical Linkage Synthesis2026

arXiv preprint, 2026-01-07, v1 · Yayati Jadhav, Amir Barati Farimani

A trajectory-conditioned causal transformer proposes linkage topology while diffusion models continuous node positions. Each added node depends on two positioned predecessors. Local retries preserve accepted prefixes; validation simulates 200 motor angles.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: One-shot kinematic validity is 29.4%; graph retries reach 96.7%, node retries 99.6%, with up to 25 retries. Mean trajectory Chamfer is 0.121, 0.145 and 0.188 respectively, measured over different valid subsets rather than matched cases.

Limits: Validity is neither target-trajectory accuracy nor solid-body feasibility. Dyadic planar mechanisms exclude general spatial assemblies; finite angle samples can miss singularities. Local retry budgets are inconsistently described elsewhere, and training/compute reporting is insufficient for confident cost estimates.

Reading: Substantial primary full-text read. sequential representation; autoregressive diffusion architecture; validation/retry algorithm; success/accuracy/diversity evaluation; embedding analysis

Contrastively aligns mechanism graphs with full and partial performance curves using ten million mechanisms. Retrieves 500 candidates, runs ten batched BFGS steps, then refines the best fifty for 150 steps. A dyadic differentiable solver optimizes dimensions while topology remains fixed.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Tests eight established trajectories, 200 in-distribution curves and 26 alphabet paths. Reports 15.49-second average synthesis in a benchmark; some comparisons use historical timings, while GCP-HOLO was rerun on matching hardware. Published table results select the best of five runs.

Limits: Training and atlas precomputation are excluded from inference timing. Complex loops are unsupported, unusual target paths remain difficult, and layer assignment does not prove complete manufacturability.

Deep Generative Model-based Synthesis of Four-bar Linkage Mechanisms with Target Conditions2024

arXiv v1, 2024-02-22; subsequently published with 'framework' in title in Journal of Computational Design and Engineering 11(5), 2024 · Sumin Lee, Jihoon Kim, Namwoo Kang

A conditional GAN generates five linkage parameters from workspace and quasi-static transmission targets. Training uses 100,000 feasible samples, a frozen performance predictor and a diversity objective. Condition sampling stays near the observed feasible joint distribution.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Across four target conditions, generated designs are more diverse than NSGA-II but less accurate on average: reported RMSE is 0.333 versus 0.278. No invalid GAN designs appeared in the bounded comparison; this is empirical, not a guarantee.

Limits: Fixed four-bar topology, normalized ground length and restricted dimensions simplify the task. Quasi-static analysis omits inertia. Sparse performance regions generalize poorly, and unbalanced diversity rewards can encourage scale growth.

Maps between mechanism drawings and colored motion curves using a shared-latent VAE. Colors encode component roles and trajectory speed. Recursive triangle construction, structural filtering and graph-isomorphism reduction produce hundreds of mechanism structures, including slider variants.

AIDL organizes structures, geometry and explicit constraints hierarchically. SolveSpace-backed recursive solving prefers rigid structural adjustment before changing internals; booleans run afterward in OpenCascade. GPT-4o receives six examples and up to five generation attempts.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Across 36 prompts and ten seeds, full AIDL has 64% generation success, compared with 94% without constraints, 77% without hierarchy and 79% for OpenSCAD. Visual similarity improves, but the evaluation centers on 2D designs and weak image metrics.

Infers joint axes and four motion types from already positioned B-Rep assemblies. Geometric contact and shared-axis tests narrow candidates; mate graphs are simplified and densified. Filters reduce 125,133 assemblies to 7,328 training candidates.

A small graph network classifies pairs of exact B-Rep entities as joint candidates. It consolidates repeated part-pair labels, recognizes equivalent axes, and searches offset, rotation and flip using overlap/contact costs.

A hierarchical sequence VAE generates cuboid construction programs with attachment and symmetry commands. Dataset extraction discovers connections, orders programs canonically and filters reconstruction failures. Semantic decoding backtracks illegal attachments.

Constructs one-DOF dyadic topologies, then samples joint positions and rejects locking motion. Reuses each topology's symbolic solution order for vectorized simulation. Coarse 50-angle filtering precedes 200-angle evaluation; curve curation reduces trivial circles and arcs.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Produces 100 million planar mechanisms and approximately 1.1 billion joint paths. Over 99% of random positions can fail for mechanisms beyond ten nodes. Simulating 10,000 mechanisms takes 454.9 seconds naively, 0.556 on 80 CPU threads, or 0.182 on one V100.

ICML 2025, PMLR 267:31249-31274 · Aleksandr Kolomeitsev, Anh-Huy Phan

Learns a shared latent space for ellipses and rounded polygons with a differentiable Heaviside field decoder plus a primitive reconstruction decoder. Compliance optimization changes latent shape, scale, placement and rotation; periodic decode/re-encode limits latent drift.

Evidence and limitations

Evidence: Across six 2D structural cases, improves compliance over ellipse and TreeTOp feature-mapping baselines, generally with less material. It remains worse than unrestricted SIMP in compliance. Twenty training runs compare decoder/latent strategies; total compute is unreported.

Uses corpus-guided branch-and-bound to discover abstractions efficiently, then rewrites programs using them. Repeated library growth is not a globally optimal search over all possible libraries.

Screened and excluded

Memory-Augmented Reinforcement Learning Agent for CAD Generation. The authors withdrew the paper on 11 August 2026 because issues in the analysis require substantial revision, and the withdrawal notice says the paper is unsuitable for citation. Its reported improvements are not used as evidence, and it is not included in the paper or reading counts.

The report was prepared as a research and business-design exercise. Sources were accessed through primary paper, author, conference and repository pages. Results from separate papers use different datasets and budgets, and no unified leaderboard is implied. No customer interviews, model training, physical experiments or application development were performed for it.
